papers.title: Thermocatalytic transcarbonation with diethyl carbonate for valorization of glycerol : recycling siliceous bauxite residue waste components and exploring the potential of sodalite hydroxide reservoir
papers.journal: Repository of the Academy's Library (Library of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences)
papers.abstract: Bauxite residues contain katoites and desilication products (sodalite and cancrinite), which are excellent candidates for Earth-abundant heterogeneous base catalysts from industrial waste sources. For the first time, they were tested in synthetizing the renewable and promising fuel or fuel additive glycerol carbonate for the purpose of recycling glycerol by-products from biodiesel production. Incorporation of silicate was found to enhance the previously established excellent catalytic activity of tricalcium aluminate (Si-free katoite). Performance of sodalites containing four different cage anion-designed (OH, CO3, SO4, Cl) and carbonated cancrinite was determined to a much greater extent by their Brönsted OH content than by the basicity of the caged anions. Direct catalytic use of bauxite residue resulted in a glycerol carbonate yield of over 80%, but it was quickly deactivated due to the limited reusability of many of its most active components (i.e., Si-free and Si-containing katoites, chloride sodalites). However, hydroxysodalites showed excellent reusability, with a glycerol carbonate yield of around 80% even after 5 reuses. The activity of katoites and sodalities overtook that of many complex systems containing relatively rare metals, such as Ni, Cu, Zr, and Ce. Their excellent activity has made it possible to use diethyl carbonate solvent/reagent, which is more favourable in terms of sustainability, instead of the more widely applied dimethyl carbonate, even with as short reaction times as 30–60 min.

papers.title: Hypoxia-responsive supramolecular systems based on macrocycles and self-assembly structures.
papers.abstract: Hypoxia is closely associated with tumor progression, metastasis, therapeutic resistance, and diagnostic challenges. The timely detection of hypoxia in live cancer cells is critical for early cancer diagnosis and for monitoring the effectiveness of anticancer therapies. Recently, there has been growing interest in non-covalent supramolecular design strategies for the development of hypoxia-sensitive sensors and prodrugs. Unlike the widely employed covalent approach, supramolecular chemistry eliminates the need for complex and time-consuming synthetic processes. Instead, the individual components of the sensor autonomously self-assemble into the desired structure. This review provides an overview of hypoxia-targeted and hypoxia-activated supramolecular probes, along with their mechanisms of action in tumor diagnosis and therapy. The supramolecular systems considered are classified according to the use of certain classes of macrocycles. The role of macrocyclic derivatives in the various proposed approaches and the response patterns of hypoxic targets will also be analyzed. Various representatives of the macrocyclic platforms, namely cyclodextrins, cucurbiturils, pillararenes, (thia)calixarenes, due to their properties such as molecular recognition, are used as molecular containers-carriers for pharmaceuticals and bio-organic fluorescent dyes. As a result of complex formation, the photostability and the signal-to-noise ratio of dyes increase. In addition, the solubility of hydrophobic guests in water improves, cytotoxicity is reduced, and targeted delivery promotes the accumulation of drugs/dyes in tumor cells.

papers.title: Nitric oxide in the occurrence and development of ischemic cerebrovascular disease.
papers.abstract: Since nitric oxide is a chemically highly reactive free radical that can act as both an oxidizing agent and a reducing agent, it is assumed that it has diverse effects on biological tissues. Nitric oxide is fundamentally important for the regulation of immune, reproductive and neuromuscular system functions and is the main signaling molecule and effector that can dilate blood vessels and modulate energy metabolism. This review examines the key role of nitric oxide in the mechanisms underlying the response to hypoxia, as well as in the effects of factors induced by hypoxia. The available conflicting information allowed us to conclude that at present, there is no consensus about the role of endogenous nitric oxide in the processes occurring after ischemic cerebrovascular disease.

papers.title: Hyperbaric oxygen for the treatment of traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
papers.abstract: The therapeutic efficacy of hyperbaric oxygen therapy for traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury remains a subject of debate. To comprehensively evaluate the impact of hyperbaric oxygen on motor function, sensory function, and activities of daily living in patients with traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury, we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis. We performed a comprehensive search across PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and major Chinese databases for randomized controlled trials published through June 2025. A total of 15 randomized controlled trials were included. The pooled results indicated that hyperbaric oxygen therapy significantly improved the American Spinal Injury Association motor score (mean difference = 10.30, 95% confidence interval: 7.70-12.90), the total American Spinal Injury Association sensory score (mean difference = 29.29, 95% confidence interval: 18.82-39.75), the American Spinal Injury Association light touch score (mean difference = 9.84, 95% confidence interval: 6.15-13.53), and the American Spinal Injury Association pinprick score (mean difference = 8.75, 95% confidence interval: 4.40-13.11). Furthermore, hyperbaric oxygen therapy was associated with significant enhancements in the Barthel Index (mean difference = 16.60, 95% confidence interval: 10.51-22.68) and the Functional Independence Measure (mean difference = 17.41, 95% confidence interval: 10.83-23.98). In conclusion, adjunctive hyperbaric oxygen therapy appears to improve motor function, sensory function, and activities of daily living in patients with traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury compared to conventional treatments alone. However, due to methodological limitations and potential publication bias in the included studies, these findings should be interpreted with caution, and further high-quality, multi-center randomized controlled trials are warranted.

papers.title: High levels of nitric oxide and peroxynitrite with protein nitration: a new therapeutic target for gliomas.
papers.abstract: The gap junction signaling pathway is a core hub mediating intercellular communication, which plays a vital role in maintaining tissue homeostasis, and its dysfunction is closely related to glioma. Nitroproteomics studies have shown that protein tyrosine nitration plays an important role in the progression of glioma, and gap junction is one of the significantly enriched nitroprotein signaling pathways in glioma; proteoformics reveals that nitration can produce various proteoforms of related proteins, which have different functional states in different subtypes of glioma, suggesting that nitration may alter the functional states of related proteins in gap junction pathways. When levels of nitric oxide and peroxynitrite (ONOO-) rise, they induce the tyrosine nitration of key proteins in the gap junction pathway; this nitration not only interferes with the function of the gap junction pathway, but also affects other gap junction-linked signaling networks. Forming an attack network on the gap junction pathway through multi-pathway cross-regulation has great potential for therapeutic strategies targeting the gap junction pathway. We recommend in-depth studies of the gap junction signaling pathway and potential drugs targeting gap junction signals, including drugs that target gap junction communication activators, nitration inhibitors, and drugs that directly target specific nitroproteins, combined with conventional chemotherapy or immune checkpoint inhibitors, as well as the construction of personalized medical frameworks as important future research directions.

papers.title: Antitrust Regulation of Algorithmic "Platform-Driven Involution'': From Governing the Corporate Person to Governing the Platform Ecosystem
papers.abstract: Digital platforms increasingly govern competition through algorithmically administered rules that allocate visibility, subsidies, commissions, participation opportunities, and sanctions. This article reconstructs ``platform-driven involution'' as a testable, portfolio-based theory-of-harm framework rather than a freestanding antitrust offense. Its application remains anchored in market definition, dominance, identified conduct under Article 22 of China's Anti-Monopoly Law, causal proof, competitive effects, and objective justification. The article clarifies that ecosystem analysis supplements rather than replaces relevant-market analysis and develops an evidence architecture for separating platform-induced effects from macroeconomic, demand, cost, and merchant-specific confounders. It then distinguishes preventive measures already supported by Chinese hard law or voluntary compliance guidance from compulsory competition-specific filing and pre-deployment assessment that would require clearer future authorization. The 2026 Trip.com decision is used to show how traffic allocation, exclusivity, lowest-price requirements, technical monitoring, and sanctions can form an integrated abuse architecture while liability remains tied to established statutory categories. Comparative analysis of EU platform regulation and Google Shopping supports calibrated procedural prevention, meaningful explanation, and causal discipline without protecting inefficient competitors or condemning aggressive competition.

The 2026 Trip.com decision is used to show how traffic allocation, exclusivity, lowest-price requirements, technical monitoring, and sanctions can form an integrated abuse architecture while liability remains tied to established statutory categories.

papers.title: Digital-Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Fault-Tolerant Control for Electrified Agricultural Machinery: A Multiphysics and Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for PMSM In-Wheel Drives
papers.abstract: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. Existing work offers mature methods for motor fault diagnosis, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and distributed-drive fault-tolerant control, but their health information is often not shared across diagnosis, maintenance, and control. This article develops a multiphysics digital-twin framework in which electrical, thermal, mechanical, and vibrational evidence maintains a probabilistic health belief that constrains both supervisory maintenance decisions and torque redistribution. The framework formalizes observability, uncertainty-aware health factors, deterministic safety shielding, multi-rate fallback logic, and agriculture-specific traction constraints. Reproducible low-fidelity numerical studies provide preliminary support for context-conditioned residual diagnosis and the revised thermal-continuity trade-off underlying health-aware derating, including robustness and sensitivity analyses. They do not validate sim-to-real transfer or the reinforcement-learning policy itself; those hypotheses remain open for dynamometer and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-performance validation.

The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-performance validation.

papers.title: Current status of room temperature magnetic compensation in impurity-doped Mn4N epitaxial thin films
papers.abstract: Mn4N, a ferrimagnet that does not contain rare-earth elements, possesses attractive properties for spintronics applications. In particular, Mn4N epitaxial films exhibit a small spontaneous magnetization of about 100 kA m(-1), a large spin polarization (p = 0.8), and large perpendicular magnetic anisotropy with a magnetic anisotropy constant of approximately 10(5) J m(-3). More importantly, achieving magnetic compensation at room temperature is possible through impurity doping. This property is particularly significant for spin-torque-based spintronics applications. In the vicinity of the magnetization and/or angular momentum compensation points, magnetization dynamics can be substantially accelerated, enabling high-speed switching and domain wall motion. This article surveys the magnetic properties of impurity-doped Mn4N epitaxial films grown on SrTiO3(001) substrates, highlighting recent results obtained with Cu-, Ag-, Au-, and Pd-doped Mn4N films in comparison with Ni- and Cr-doped Mn4N films. Furthermore, with a view to device applications of Mn4N, we present the formation of ultrathin (similar to 4 nm) Pt epitaxial films with a <100> orientation on MgO (001), which is essential for injecting spins into Mn4N-based overlayers by utilizing the spin Hall effect of heavy metals. papers.title: Reproducible chiroptical activity from aggregated chiral thienopyrroledione-fluorene π-conjugated polymers
papers.abstract: Chiral pi-conjugated polymers have attracted considerable interest because their chiral-aggregated structures can generate pronounced chiroptical responses. Here, we report the design, synthesis, and chiroptical characterization of fluorene - thienopyrroledione polymers bearing a single chiral center in each repeating unit, (R)- and (S)-PFTPD, prepared via direct arylation polycondensation to minimize structural defects. Although only weak chiroptical activity was observed in the solution, the addition of 1-butanol to CHCl3 solutions of the polymers induced the formation of stable aggregates that exhibited strong circular dichroism (CD) and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL). Systematic examination of the sample preparation parameters revealed that the mixing process critically influences the chiroptical properties. Dropwise addition of 1-butanol under controlled stirring provided the most reliable results, yielding highly reproducible CD spectra. Under these optimized conditions, the aggregates exhibited an average dissymmetry factor (|g abs|) of 1.5 & times; 10-2 and a CPL dissymmetry factor (|g lum|) of 1.9 & times; 10-2. These values rank among the highest reported for pi-conjugated polymer aggregates bearing only a single chiral source per repetition unit. This study demonstrates that precise control over the solvent-mixing process is essential for the reproducible emergence of chiroptical properties and highlights the chiral TPD unit as a promising platform for chiroptical polymer materials.

papers.title: Somatosensory phenotyping in women with persistent genital arousal disorder: a case-control study.
papers.abstract: Introduction: Persistent genital arousal disorder (PGAD) is a rare and distressing condition characterized by persistent, unwanted genital arousal in the absence of sexual desire or stimulation. Persistent genital arousal disorder is increasingly recognized as a disorder of abnormal genital sensory processing, but objective neurophysiological data remain limited. Methods: We conducted an exploratory case-control study to characterize somatosensory function in women with PGAD. Thirty women with PGAD and 30 age-matched healthy controls were recruited at Leiden University Medical Center. Participants underwent quantitative sensory testing (QST) at hand and external genital sites, conditioned pain modulation, and corneal confocal microscopy. Results: Hand QST values were within normal range in both groups. In the genital region, PGAD participants showed altered thermal pain processing, with cold and heat hyperalgesia compared with controls. Mechanical pain thresholds did not differ between groups; however, PGAD participants reported higher pain intensity ratings to mechanical stimuli and showed significantly greater temporal summation of pain in genital regions. Genital dynamic mechanical allodynia occurred more frequently in PGAD participants but did not differ significantly at the group level. Conditioned pain modulation magnitude did not differ between groups and showed substantial interindividual variability. Corneal confocal microscopy abnormalities were observed in a proportion of participants in both groups without significant between-group differences. Discussion: These findings show that QST is feasible in women with PGAD and indicate that PGAD is associated with altered somatosensory processing demonstrating genital thermal hypersensitivity and central pain sensitization in a subset of patients.

papers.title: Enhancing mass transport in redox flow batteries with 3D-printed triply periodic minimal surface electrode structures
papers.abstract: Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structures offer a compelling route for designing porous electrodes with tunable architectures for electrochemical applications such as redox flow batteries. In this study, we fabricated carbonaceous TPMS electrodes, including gyroid, diamond, IWP, and cubic geometries, using digital light processing, and evaluated their performance in single-electrolyte flow cells using an organic redox couple. The printing process and subsequent thermal treatment produced conductive porous electrodes that closely replicated the intended TPMS geometries, preserving the characteristic features of each design. Through a detailed analysis of pressure drop, surface area, and electrochemical behavior, we identified the diamond design as particularly effective in enhancing mass transport while maintaining low hydraulic resistance. We further assessed gyroid structures, selected for being the most well-known among TPMSs, across a range of porosities, finding that higher porosity improved flow performance despite a reduction in surface area, an advantageous trade-off for electrolytes with facile kinetics and low ionic conductivity. Comparison with a commercial carbon felt electrode revealed comparable ohmic resistance and favorable flow characteristics, though reduced electrochemical surface area limited the achievable current densities. To isolate mass transport effects, a kinetically facile organic redox couple was employed, after which a representative 3D-printed gyroid electrode was evaluated in a proof-of-concept full-cell vanadium redox flow battery. A full-cell test demonstrated the feasibility of printed electrodes, achieving a voltage efficiency of 76% at a current density of 50 mA cm−2. These findings demonstrate the potential of architected 3D printed electrodes for future redox flow batteries and highlight the importance of tuning geometry and porosity to balance power output, mass transport, and system-level pumping losses.

papers.title: Airdrop Sybil Attack detection framework supported by machine learning
papers.journal: International Journal of Electronics and Telecommunication Systems
papers.abstract: A skilled hunter may earn thousands of dollars in tokens from a single airdrop, making airdrop Sybil assaults a profitable endeavor. In this situation, Sybil assaults are not always wanted by projects and are often seen as improper behavior by honest individuals, which may negatively impact a project's image. It is thus to be anticipated that detection methods for Sybil assaults would be continuously enhanced. This study presents a multistep structure. Its concept is to sort blockchain addresses and give each one a score that indicates whether it belongs to the Sybil or regular class. Topologies were classified using a graph isomorphism network, whose parameters were adjusted using a dataset that the authors labeled. In subsequent phases, the account clustering operation was performed using a DBSCAN. Each stage in the framework may be given arbitrary weights by users, which will decide how essential a step is to them and provide a different score for a particular address. A grid search strategy and a threshold after which the address is deemed Sybil were used to find the optimal weights. This article examined a collection of EOAs from the ZK sync rollup. Ultimately, 76% of the examined accounts were classified as Sybils. Compared to the official ZK sync eligibility list, we found 342 addresses that received airdrop tokens but were marked as Sybil by our solution.

papers.title: DIAGNOSTIC ACCURACY OF ULTRA-LOW-DOSE CT VS. STANDARD-DOSE CT FOR PULMONARY NODULE DETECTION: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS
authors: KHALED BONNA , RASHA GALAL ELSAFTY , NORA EID ALANAZI , RANIN JABER M ALMAJRASHI AHLAM ALI Y ASIRI , WALEED MUFAREH ALSHAHRANI , SOMAYYAH SOHAIL MITHA , SHOUG NASSER ALKHAMMASH , BANDAR SAAD ALSHREEF
papers.journal: TPM Testing, psychometrics, methodology in applied psychology
papers.abstract: Background: Standard dose computed tomography (CT) is a primary modality for detecting pulmonary nodules (PNs), but the health risk from cumulative radiation exposure has prompted the emergence of ultra-low-dose CT (ULDCT) as an alternative to reduce this dose, because its diagnostic accuracy remains variable, this systematic review and meta-analysis aims to synthesize the existing evidence to determine the diagnostic accuracy and effective radiation dose of ULDCT for pulmonary nodule detection. Methods: Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Ovid MEDLINE for original research published between 2015 and 2025 that evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of ULDCT for PN detection, for which a meta-analysis using random-effects models was performed to calculate the pooled sensitivity for nodule detection and the pooled mean effective radiation dose, with a subgroup analysis conducted to assess the impact of different reconstruction algorithms. Results: Forty-two studies comprising 15,792 patients were included, from which a meta-analysis of 11 studies demonstrated a pooled sensitivity of 91.9% (95% CI: 84.6%–97.1%) for PN detection with heterogeneity (I²=93.0%), and a pooled mean effective dose from 12 studies of 0.22 mSv (95% CI: 0.11–0.33 mSv), a level comparable to standard chest radiography, while subgroup analysis revealed a trend towards higher sensitivity with advanced reconstruction algorithms (96.7%) compared to standard iterative reconstruction (87.9%) that was not statistically significant (p=0.091), and a narrative synthesis confirmed ULDCT's accuracy for solid nodules but identified reduced sensitivity for subsolid, ground-glass, and small (<6 mm) nodules, with performance limited in patients with a high body mass index (BMI). Conclusion: ULDCT combined with advanced reconstruction techniques offers high diagnostic accuracy for the detection of solid pulmonary nodules and reduces radiation exposure to levels approaching that of a chest X-ray, but its utility is limited for detecting subsolid and small nodules and in obese patients, making protocol standardization and patient-specific considerations essential to optimize its clinical implementation.

papers.title: Management rather than climate and biodiversity shapes long-term delta15N dynamics in grassland soils
papers.abstract: The bulk soil δ 15 N signature in grassland soils serves as a fingerprint of nitrogen inputs, turnover and losses, reflecting the influence of land management, climate, plant biodiversity and abiotic soil properties.Although natural abundance δ 15 N has been proposed as an indicator for these factors, previous studies yielded mixed results regarding the importance of its drivers.In this study, we quantified changes in soil δ 15 N across 72 German grassland sites after 12 years (2011 vs. 2023) and analysed relationships with detailed records of land use intensity, plant biodiversity, climate, and soil properties.Land use intensity was quantified on a continuous scale based on mowing, grazing and fertilisation.In the top 10 cm of soil, δ 15 N changes ranged from -0.86 to + 2.49‰, equating to an average increase of + 0.35‰ per decade.Over two-thirds of our study sites showed a long-term increase in δ 15 N associated with high land use intensity.Our findings indicate that fertiliser application and grazing are the dominant drivers of δ 15 N increases, while a biodiversity-mediated decrease via reduced N losses was not observed.The slow decadal-scale shifts suggest that single soil δ 15 N measurements without known initial values are only informative for long-term management processes and not for assessing recent management impacts.

papers.title: A Quantitative Framework for Assessing Digital Sovereignty
papers.journal: UPM Digital Archive (Technical University of Madrid)
papers.abstract: Digital sovereignty is a political buzzword. However, there are diverging views on how to define and measure it. Throughout this study we propose the creation of a quantitative framework to measure digital sovereignty capabilities on a country's performance in three key areas: technology, government, and users. Through our analysis covering 123 countries, we have shown the different paths towards achieving sovereignty that are imprinted into how the countries contribute to the digital economy and reflect the asymmetries existing in the global value chains. The US and China both show a strong technological leadership, especially regarding emerging technologies, while the EU maintains a balance between innovation and regulations that the new strategies and MFF must address in order to become a relevant global player.

papers.title: Effects of Thermal Induction on the Structural and Functional Properties of Bamboo Shoot Protein
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: To develop novel plant protein resources and enhance the high-value utilization of bamboo shoot processing by-products, bamboo shoot protein (BSP) was extracted using ammonium sulfate precipitation. The effects of different heat treatment temperatures (room temperature, 50, 75 and 100 ℃) on the structural and functional properties of BSP were systematically evaluated. The results showed that heat treatment markedly altered the structural properties of BSP. SDS-PAGE analysis revealed that thermal treatment facilitated the aggregation of BSP, while scanning electron microscopy (SEM) indicated that the spherical protein particles became loose and porous after heating. Particle size and Zeta potential analyses showed that BSP treated at 50 ℃ exhibited the smallest particle size (1024.5 nm) and the highest absolute Zeta potential (14.42 mV), indicating good dispersion stability. In terms of chemical characteristics, the free sulfhydryl (-SH) content decreased with increasing temperature, while the water and oil binding capacities increased. In addition, BSP treated at 50 ℃ showed the highest foaming capacity (108.00%) and foam stability (37.24%). Thermogravimetric analysis (TG) and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) further demonstrated that BSP treated at 50 ℃ exhibited enhanced thermal stability; meanwhile, BSP exhibited good free radical scavenging capacity and reducing power. In conclusion, moderate heat treatment at 50 ℃ improves the structural and functional properties of BSP, providing a theoretical basis for its application in food processing.

papers.title: Structural Characterization and Prebiotic Activity of Selenized Polysaccharide from Passiflora edulis Peel
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: To investigate the potential of acid-extracted polysaccharides from the peel of Passiflora edulis Sims (APEP) as prebiotics, the APEP were complexed with sodium selenite. The selenized acid-extracted polysaccharide from Passiflora edulis Sims peel (APEP-Se) was successfully prepared. The physicochemical properties of APEP and APEP-Se were characterized. The structural characteristics of the samples were examined using a variety of analytical methods, including ultraviolet scanning, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, Congo red staining, thermogravimetric analysis, and scanning electron microscopy. The present study was conducted to ascertain the effects of APEP and APEP-Se on the growth of Lactobacillus plantarum, Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus, Lactobacillus brevis, and Streptococcus thermophilus. The physicochemical analysis revealed that, in comparison with APEP, APEP-Se exhibited increased uronic acid content but reduced total sugar content, protein content, and solubility. The selenium content of APEP-Se was 932.70±29.59 µg/g, thereby confirming the successful preparation of the selenated polysaccharide. Structural characterization indicated that both APEP and APEP-Se are composed of seven monosaccharides: Man, Rha, GlcA, GalA, Glc, Gal, and Ara, with Glc being the main component. After selenylation modification, the molecular weight of APEP-Se decreased from 281.05 kDa to 210.02 kDa. The infrared spectrum exhibited characteristic absorption peaks indicative of polysaccharides and selenylation modification. Additionally, the structure transitioned from lacking a triple-helical conformation to possessing a triple-helical structure, while thermal stability improved and the external morphology changed. Prebiotic experiments demonstrated that both APEP and APEP-Se effectively promoted the proliferation and metabolic activities of four probiotic strains—Lactobacillus plantarum, Lactobacillus delbrueckii (subsp.) bulgaricus, Lactobacillus brevis, and Streptococcus thermophilus—thereby exhibiting certain prebiotic effects. This study provides a theoretical foundation for the prebiotic application of selenium-enriched polysaccharides from Passiflora edulis peel, offers insights for developing them into novel functional foods, and indirectly promotes the resource reuse of the fruit peel.

papers.title: SYNTHESIS, CHARACTERIZATION, AND CATALYTIC ACTIVITY OF ZNZRO₃ MIXED METAL OXIDE FOR METHYLENE BLUE OXIDATION
authors: Ibraheem Asaad Ismaeel Zeina Loai Al-Yousef*
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Zinc zirconate (ZnZrO₃) is a mixed-metal oxide with potential applications in heterogeneous catalysis and advanced oxidation processes. In the present study, ZnZrO₃ was synthesized by the sol-gel method under the optimized experimental conditions previously established and reported by the authors.[1] The synthesized material was subjected to thermal treatment at different temperatures and characterized using differential thermal analysis (DTA), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR) to investigate its thermal behavior, phase evolution, and structural characteristics. The catalytic activity of ZnZrO₃ was evaluated for the oxidative degradation of methylene blue (MB) in the presence of hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) under heterogeneous catalytic conditions. For comparison, NiZrO₃, which had previously been synthesized and characterized by the sol-gel method according to the authors’ earlier work[2], was evaluated under the same catalytic conditions. The results showed that the ZnZrO₃ phase was formed at high calcination temperatures, with the ZnZrO₃ phase obtained at 1000 °C. The catalytic experiments demonstrated that ZnZrO₃ exhibited higher catalytic efficiency toward MB oxidation than NiZrO₃, with catalytic efficiencies of 58.33% and 28.57%, respectively. These findings indicate that ZnZrO₃ possesses promising catalytic activity for the heterogeneous oxidative treatment of methylene blue using hydrogen peroxide and demonstrate its potential as a mixed-metal oxide catalyst for advanced oxidation applications.

papers.title: DEVELOPMENT AND OPTIMIZATION OF CURCUMIN UFASOMAL VAGINAL GEL USING DoE APPROACH
authors: Chaithanya Nagesh*1 Dr. J. Adlin Jino Nesalin1
papers.abstract: The present study aimed to develop and characterize a Curcumin-loaded ufasomal vaginal gel for vaginal cancer therapy to enhance drug permeation and therapeutic efficacy. Curcumin, a BCS Class IV drug with low solubility and permeability, was incorporated into ufasomes using the ethanol injection method. A Central Composite Design (CCD) was employed to optimize formulation variables, including oleic acid, Span 60, and cholesterol concentrations. The optimized formulation was evaluated for entrapment efficiency, particle size, zeta potential, in vitro drug release, and vesicle morphology. The optimized ufasomal formulation exhibited an entrapment efficiency of 61.8 ± 0.012%, particle size of 138 nm, zeta potential of 8.5 mV, and drug release of 78.2 ± 0.859% after 8 hours. FTIR and DSC studies confirmed the absence of drug–excipient interactions, while SEM revealed spherical vesicles with smooth morphology. The vaginal gel formulation showed desirable pH, viscosity, spreadability, and drug-content uniformity. These results suggest that the developed Curcumin-loaded ufasomal vaginal gel provides controlled drug release and could serve as a promising vaginal delivery system for improving the therapeutic efficacy of Curcumin in vaginal cancer.

papers.title: Voltage–Current-Emission Framework of Time-Resolved Electroluminescence
papers.abstract: Abstract Time-resolved electroluminescence has been a central methodology for the development of LED devices. However, it still lacks quantitative theoretical descriptions of time-resolved electroluminescence. By combining the equivalent circuit models of semiconductor devices and the carrier dynamics of electroluminescence processes, here we have developed a voltage–current-emission framework to illustrate time-resolved electroluminescence from the pulse voltage as input, to injection current, and finally generate electroluminescence as output. The features of different LED devices can be quantitatively interpreted, confirming their universal applicability across LEDs with different materials and device structures. Importantly, the curves of time-resolved electroluminescence can be simulated to quantitatively describe the dynamics of current and carriers of the LED operation. In all, the voltage–current–emission framework offers theoretical guidance for achieving advanced LED devices for artificial intelligence (AI) technology.

papers.title: Quantum-logic spectroscopy of forbidden vibrational transitions in single nitrogen molecular ions
papers.abstract: Abstract Electric-dipole forbidden spectroscopic transitions in atoms form the basis of many advanced implementations of quantum computers, atomic clocks and quantum sensors. Coherently addressing such transitions in molecules which are among the most ubiquitous and versatile quantum objects has remained a long-standing challenge owing to their complex energy-level structure. Here, we report the search, observation and coherent manipulation of electric-quadrupole rotational-vibrational transitions in single trapped molecules using a quantum-logic-spectroscopy protocol. We identify individual hyperfine-Zeeman-rotational components of the fundamental vibrational transition of the nitrogen molecular ion, $${{{{{\rm{N}}}}}}_{2}^{+}$$ N 2 + , and perform coherent population transfer between energy levels. Our work opens up new perspectives for precision molecular spectroscopy, for high-fidelity qubits encoded in the rotational-vibrational motion of molecules, for precise infrared molecular clocks and for searches for new physics.

papers.title: X-ray Crystallography of a Nanobody/JAM-1 Complex Informs Barrier Weakening and Enhanced Drug Permeability in a Cellular Blood–Brain Barrier Model
papers.abstract: Abstract For pharmacological treatments of brain disorders, the blood–brain barrier (BBB) poses a formidable obstacle, tightly restricting the cerebral uptake of therapeutic agents. Tight junction (TJ) binders, including peptides, proteins, and monoclonal antibodies, that specifically bind to the extracellular domains (ECDs) of TJ proteins are increasingly being explored as BBB-weakening agents for enhanced drug delivery to the brain. Given that nanobodies (Nbs) can access epitopes that are often inaccessible to conventional antibodies, we obtained 16 Nbs with unique CDRs via immunization of alpaca with the ECD of either human (h) or murine JAM-1 (mJAM-1), a major TJ protein. Twelve Nb candidates exhibited high-affinity binding to mJAM-1, as measured by surface plasmon resonance (SPR), and these interactions were further validated for 9 Nbs by immunostaining of JAM-1-overexpressing cells. Five Nbs were found to weaken the barrier of the eGFP-hCldn5-MDCKII cellular monolayer, as shown by reduced transendothelial electrical resistance (TEER). X-ray crystallography revealed that the lead barrier-weakening Nb, E6, binds to the membrane-proximal nondimeric D2 domain of mJAM-1. Mutating key residues at this interface eliminated the BBB-weakening effect of E6, as evidenced by unaltered sodium fluorescence (NaFI) leakage in both eGFP-hCldn5-MDCKII and mJAM1-mGL-MDCKII cellular monolayers compared with the nontreated control. Our study highlights the potential of JAM-1-targeting Nbs as BBB modulators, offering a promising approach for generating TJ binders to enhance brain drug delivery.

papers.title: Unveiling the binding dynamics of banana lectin with L-fucose through integrative spectroscopic, crystallographic, and in silico studies
papers.abstract: Banana lectin (Banlec) is a homodimeric plant lectin with glucose/mannose specificity and is also capable of recognizing other carbohydrates. The present study was conducted to evaluate the binding modalities of Banlec with L -fucose. Such structural and biophysical characterization is essential for understanding the molecular basis of Banlec–carbohydrate recognition and its potential applications in glycobiology. Banlec was purified from Musa paradisiaca , and its binding with L -fucose was analyzed via different biophysical techniques. In the first step, the binding affinity of Banlec with L-fucose was analyzed via UV–Vis spectroscopy, which revealed a decreased absorption intensity at 280 nm with increasing concentrations of L-fucose. The binding constant (K b = (4.78 ± 0.08) ×10 4 M −1 ), dissociation constant (K d =21.8 ± 0.3 µM), and Gibbs free energy (ΔG°= − 26.7 kJ mol −1 ), suggest a favourable interaction. Results of circular dichroism spectroscopic (CD) analysis showed that binding of fucose did not alter the secondary structure of Banlec. Differential scanning fluorimetry showed a slight increase in melting temperature (ΔTm = + 0.5 °C) upon L -fucose binding. Additionally, the X-ray crystal structure of Banlec–fucose complex was resolved at 2.95 Å. Two molecules of L -fucose showed binding with Ser33, Gly34, His63, His84, and Gly105 amino acid residues. Molecular docking studies further supported the experimental findings. Hence, this study provides structural insights into the carbohydrate-binding features of Banlec, particularly its interaction with L-fucose.

Two molecules of L -fucose showed binding with Ser33, Gly34, His63, His84, and Gly105 amino acid residues.

papers.title: Role of bio-polymeric binders on combustion and fire suppression performance of KNO3/KClO4–3,5 DNB pyrotechnic composite
papers.abstract: Traditional pyrotechnic composites (PCs), often synthesized with epoxy or other synthetic binders, can combust at temperatures up to ​ 2100 °C, creating secondary fire and explosion risks. This study examines how renewable, cost-effective binders: starch, guar gum, tannic acid, and sodium carboxymethyl cellulose affect the combustion behavior, exothermicity, temperature profiles, and fire-suppression performance of PCs in a 4.57 kW n-heptane pool fire. Characterization of the aerosol particulates was performed using XRD, FTIR, and SEM. SEM-EDX and DSC for the PCs. PC-1, with a linear burning rate (LBR) of 10.05 ± 2.158 mm/s, extinguished the fire within 5 s and generated the highest ignition temperature (210 °C), whereas PC-4 and PC-5 with LBRs of 9.3 ± 0.742 mm/s and 9.7 ± 0.693 mm/s, respectively showed a noticeable decrease in ignition temperatures (184 °C and 182 °C, respectively) and suppressed the fire within 7 s and 5 s, respectively. It can be concluded that starch-based PC exhibited optimal fire performance parameters, making it a promising bio-based binder for the KNO 3 -KClO 4 -3, 5 DNB pyrotechnic composition.

papers.title: Piracetam attenuates cyclophosphamide-evoked pulmonary injury in rats; the role of AMPK/NF-κB/NLRP3/caspase-1 and caspase-3 mediated apoptosis signaling cascades
papers.abstract: Abstract Cyclophosphamide (CP) is often employed in the treatment of numerous malignancies and autoimmune diseases, although it is accompanied by numerous side effects. Piracetam (PIRA) is used as a nootropic agent and reported to possess antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-apoptotic properties in addition to its established cognitive-enhancing effects. This study aimed to investigate the potential protective effects of PIRA against CP-induced lung damage in rats. CP was utilized to provoke pulmonary damage. Molecular docking was performed to predict the binding affinity of piracetam for NF-κB p65, NLRP3, caspase-1, caspase-3, and AMPK. Arterial blood gas parameters (PaO₂ and PaCO₂) were assessed to evaluate pulmonary gas-exchange function. The lung contents of MDA, GSH, and CAT activity were measured. Levels of lung IL-18, IL-1β, TNF-α, and caspase-1 were evaluated using ELISA. Immunohistochemistry was employed to evaluate NF-κB p65 and caspase-3. The Western blot technique was utilized to evaluate the protein expression of NLRP3 and p-AMPK. Lung Bax and Bcl-2 gene expression was assessed using qRT-PCR. The histological examination of lung tissues was conducted. Molecular docking revealed favorable binding affinities of piracetam. CP caused a notable reduction in PaO₂ and elevation in PaCO₂, alongside a notable increase in lung MDA, IL-18, IL-1β, TNF-α, caspase-1, and Bax levels, with a substantial reduction in GSH, CAT, p-AMPK, and Bcl-2. CP administration also led to the upregulation of NLRP3 protein. Additionally, the immunopositivity of both NF-κB p65 and caspase-3 was elevated in the CP group. PIRA markedly ameliorated all previously described functional, biochemical, and histopathological anomalies. PIRA pretreatment significantly improved CP-induced pulmonary injury, an effect associated with suppression of NF-κB/NLRP3/caspase-1 and caspase-3 signaling and with increased p-AMPK expression.

This study aimed to investigate the potential protective effects of PIRA against CP-induced lung damage in rats. Levels of lung IL-18, IL-1β, TNF-α, and caspase-1 were evaluated using ELISA.

papers.title: Precision maize crop height mapping using multispectral and LiDAR data from unmanned aerial system
papers.abstract: Abstract Context Spatially explicit and accurate maize crop height maps are essential for supporting site-specific management in precision agriculture. Although low-cost unmanned aerial system (UAS)-based multispectral imagery offers a promising approach for maize crop height estimation, it’s accuracy under varying canopy conditions remains uncertain. Aims In this study, we used 3D point clouds to estimate maize crop height during sparse and dense canopy cover based on UAS-captured multispectral images and compare with light detection and ranging (LiDAR)-based estimates. Methods The 3D point clouds from multispectral images and LiDAR data were processed using a spatially localized grid (SLG) filtering approachto derive digital terrain model (DTM) and canopy surface model (CSM), which were then used to estimate maize crop height.Furthermore, two strategies were explored — (1) grid expansion, and (2) using ground reference derived during sparse canopy aspotential tools to mitigate issues during dense canopy cover for multispectral image-based estimations. Results Results showed that the crop height estimated from multispectral images during sparse canopy cover show comparable accuracy (r = 0.9, nRMSE = 32%) to LiDAR-based estimation (r = 0.81, nRMSE = 17%). The accuracy of multispectral-based estimation, however, significantly declined under dense canopy cover, where no meaningful correlation was observed (r = − 0.1, nRMSE = 61%). In contrast, LiDAR-based estimates show consistent level of accuracy under the same conditions (r = 0.78, nRMSE = 15%). When grid expansion strategy was implemented for multispectral-based estimation during the dense canopy cover, the nRMSE was observed to decrease up to 28%. Meanwhile, with the use of sparse canopy cover ground reference, the nRMSE decreased up to 17%, comparable to the LiDAR-based estimate. Conclusion Overall, these results demonstrate the potential of deriving crop heights cost-effectively using multispectral imaging from UAS. This approach offers a scalable and economically viable alternative to expensive LiDAR systems, enabling wider integration of crop height information into precision agriculture applications.

papers.title: Fabrication and characterization of Fe 3 O 4 -reinforced PEG–PCL magnetic shape memory nanofibers
papers.abstract: Abstract In this study, magnetic shape memory nanofibers based on PEG–PCL (1:1) reinforced with Fe 3 O 4 nanoparticles were produced using the electrospinning method. The structural properties of the nanofibers were analyzed using X-ray diffraction (XRD) and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), while their surface morphologies were examined using atomic force microscopy (AFM) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Thermal properties were determined using differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), while magnetic behavior was assessed with a physical property measurement system (PPMS). XRD results indicated that Fe 3 O 4 nanoparticles were homogeneously distributed in the matrix, with an increased contribution from the magnetic crystal phase. FTIR indicated that the additive was integrated into the structure via physical interactions, without establishing chemical bonds with the polymer chains. Based on SEM and AFM images, the fiber diameters have grown significantly as the Fe 3 O 4 content has increased. TGA analyses indicate that the thermal stability of nanocomposites has increased, while DSC results demonstrate that as the filler amount increases, the degree of polymer crystallization decreases. Magnetic measurements have shown that saturation magnetization increases with dopant and that composites transition from diamagnetic to ferromagnetic behavior. It has also been found that nanofibers show shape memory properties when heated.

TGA analyses indicate that the thermal stability of nanocomposites has increased, while DSC results demonstrate that as the filler amount increases, the degree of polymer crystallization decreases. It has also been found that nanofibers show shape memory properties when heated.

papers.title: High-Pressure Solid–Liquid Equilibrium and Volumetric Behavior of Choline Chloride-Based Eutectic Solvents
papers.abstract: Abstract Over the past two decades, eutectic solvents (ESs) have attracted attention due to their potential in various fields, from chemical processing to materials science. Despite this growing interest, their use is still restricted to fixed stoichiometric mole ratios. This limitation arises from the difficulty in accurately identifying eutectic compositions, a consequence of the scarcity of reliable thermophysical property data. In particular, properties such as density and solid–liquid equilibrium (SLE) remain poorly documented in the literature, especially under elevated pressure. In this context, this work reports SLE and volumetric data for mixtures of choline chloride with four hydrogen-bond donors: ethylene glycol, glycerol, 1,3-propanediol, and glycolic acid. SLE measurements were performed in the pressure range between 6 MPa and 25 MPa and compared with available data at atmospheric pressure. Density measurements were carried out for the ESs at their eutectic compositions over ranges of pressure (5 MPa to 50 MPa) and temperature (293.15 K to 353.15 K). The experimental density data were correlated using the modified Tammann–Tait equation, yielding average relative deviations below 0.45 %. Based on the fitted parameters, the isothermal compressibility ( $${\kappa}_{T}$$ κ T ) and the isobaric thermal expansivity ( $${\alpha}_{T}$$ α T ) were calculated. Both properties exhibited dependence on pressure and temperature, in agreement with the behavior of incompressible liquid systems. This study enlarges the thermodynamic database of ChCl-based ESs by providing the first high-pressure SLE data along with new volumetric measurements. These results improve the understanding of ES phase behavior and offer valuable inputs for thermodynamic modeling, process design, and the development of ES-based applications.

papers.title: Effect of reduced graphene oxide and maleic anhydride compatibilization on the curing, morphological, and pre-/post-aging mechanical properties of EPDM/NBR blends
papers.abstract: Abstract This study investigates the development of elastomeric composites based on ethylene-propylene-diene monomer (EPDM) and nitrile-butadiene rubber (NBR) reinforced with reduced graphene oxide (rGO). Given the limited literature on the combined use of rGO and compatibilizing agents in EPDM/NBR systems, this research focused on the effect of a maleic anhydride-grafted ethylene elastomer (E–g-MA) in EPDM, NBR and a 70/30 EPDM/NBR blend prepared using two-roll mill mixing. The rGO was characterized through X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) with quantitative energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy and thermogravimetric analysis, while the elastomer compounds were evaluated for cure characteristics, morphology, chemical resistance and mechanical properties before and after accelerated aging. SEM micrographs revealed that the combination of E–g-MA and rGO reduced the number of pull-out voids and produced a more homogeneous fracture surface in EPDM and in the EPDM/NBR blend. At higher E–g-MA and rGO content (1 phr), tensile strength improved 127% for EPDM and 81% for the blend, and the elongation at break of EPDM increased from 216 to 490%. Welch's ANOVA with Games-Howell post-hoc tests (α = 0.05) confirmed that these differences are statistically significant. For NBR, neither additive significantly changed the tensile properties, although 1 phr of rGO reduced the volume change in propanone from 70 to 41%. After accelerated aging, EPDM/NBR/1E-g-MA/1rGO reached a tensile strength of 5.1 MPa, compared with 2.2 MPa for the neat blend. This composite also showed a lower volume change than the neat blend after immersion (16% versus 31% in propanone and 194% versus 229% in fuel oil), whereas EPDM/1E-g-MA/1rGO showed increased swelling in propanone. These findings indicate that combining rGO and E–g-MA is an effective strategy for improving the strength and aging behavior of EPDM/NBR composites, although the reduced resistance of EPDM to polar solvents at the highest loading should be considered.

papers.title: DBAASP V4: condition-resolved bioactivity and chemical structures for data-driven peptide and peptidomimetic discovery
papers.abstract: The current peptide renaissance-driven by metagenomic and proteomic mining, molecular de-extinction, protein language models, and generative or evolutionary design-is producing millions of candidates, but useful machine learning depends on experimentally anchored, context-rich labels. The Database of Antimicrobial Activity and Structure of Peptides (DBAASP) is a manually curated resource linking peptides and peptidomimetics to quantitative antimicrobial, antibiofilm, anticancer, hemolytic, and mammalian-cell cytotoxicity measurements and their experimental conditions. DBAASP v4 contains >25 000 entries and extends the resource from a sequence-centered database to a structure-aware repository. Major additions include systematic SMILES representations, enhanced annotation of intrachain bonds and ring architectures, dedicated antibiofilm, and synergy records, PubChem links, >9200 molecular-dynamics trajectories, and new prediction services. The condition-resolved data support supervised learning, strain-, and target-specific models, model calibration, and surrogate fitness functions for genetic algorithms. SMILES representations further enable modeling of noncanonical peptides and peptidomimetics that cannot be adequately described by sequence alone. DBAASP therefore complements large peptide catalogues by providing the experimentally curated activity and structure layers, needed to convert sequence information into testable predictions, design, and optimization of biologically active compounds. DBAASP v4 is freely available at https://dbaasp.org.

papers.title: A comprehensive review of computational strategies in the rational design of biosensors based on allosteric transcription factors for pollutant detection
papers.abstract: Allosteric transcription factor (aTF)-based biosensors are powerful analytical tools for the detection of different analytes such as environmental pollutants and are widely used in medical diagnostics and environmental monitoring. These biosensors rely on ligand-induced conformational changes in transcription factors that regulate gene expression, thereby positioning them as low-cost, sensitive and selective components in biosensor design. In recent times, computational biology and chemistry techniques such as homology modelling, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, free energy perturbation (FEP), enhanced sampling techniques and machine learning have been widely employed in the design and optimization of aTF-based biosensors. With these methods, the structures of proteins could be predicted, the ligand-binding pockets could be identified and characterized, the interactions therein could be analyzed and binding affinities could be predicted. Also, the conformational dynamics, allosteric and transition pathways, free energy landscapes, relative binding free energies of the ligand-aTF complexes can be predicted. Taken together, these can facilitate the engineering of aTFs with improved sensitivity and specificity. Therefore, this review highlights the individual and complementary roles of these computational techniques in the design and optimization of aTF-based biosensors and discusses the recent advances, current limitations and future directions in the design of next-generation aTF-based biosensors.

papers.title: A hybrid transformer and Mamba network with mixture of experts for deformable multimodal 3D medical image registration
papers.abstract: Deformable 3D multimodal medical image registration is a fundamental yet challenging task that requires accurate alignment of volumetric image pairs acquired from different imaging modalities, such as MRI and CT or MRI and TRUS, where large appearance differences, structural variability, and geometric misalignment make correspondence estimation particularly difficult. We propose DH-TMReg, a weakly supervised deformable cross-modality hybrid registration framework that integrates a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) bottleneck to achieve accurate and robust 3D multimodal volumetric alignment. The architecture couples a Swin Transformer (ST) branch processing the fixed image and a Mamba Vision (MV) state-space model branch processing the moving image through a sequential cross-fusion strategy that progressively enriches each modality with complementary representations from the other across four hierarchical levels. To address the inherent geometric inconsistency between unregistered multimodal 3D image pairs, Deformable Cross-modal self-attention Fusion Skip Connections (DCASC) are applied at every encoder level to adaptively realign and fuse spatially inconsistent dual-branch features through learned deformable sampling offsets. At the bottleneck, a MoE module with top-2 gating over 8 expert networks dynamically routes features through specialized sub-networks to increase representational capacity without proportional computational overhead. Extensive experiments on two challenging 3D multimodal registration benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving a mean Dice score of 0.837 ± 0.077 and ASSD of 3.386 ± 1.696 mm on the prostate MRI/TRUS dataset, and a mean Dice score of 0.9451 ± 0.0079 and ASSD of 0.916 ± 0.286 mm on the abdominal MRI/CT dataset, outperforming state-of-the-art multimodal registration methods on held-out test data.

papers.title: Human PSC-Derived Cardiac Cells for Heart Failure: From Cell Therapy to Engineered Tissue Patches
papers.journal: Current Treatment Options in Cardiovascular Medicine
papers.abstract: Abstract Purpose of Review This comprehensive overview evaluates recent progress in human pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocyte therapies to improve the outcome of heart failure patients, with emphasis on delivery routes, early clinical employment, and the barriers for sustained functional cardiac repair. Recent Findings Multiple complementary strategies for cardiac remuscularization are being pursued in parallel, including single cell suspension, multicellular spheroids, cardiomyocyte sheets, and engineered myocardial tissues. Early clinical translation has established feasibility across several platforms, while engineered heart muscle has provided the clearest evidence of persistent graft retention and structural myocardial augmentation. Cardiomyocyte sheets have reached conditional regulatory approval, and catheter-based spheroid delivery is entering clinical evaluation. However, arrhythmogenicity, immune rejection, incomplete maturation and manufacturing complexity remain major challenges on the path to the clinic. Summary Pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiac products are transitioning from experimental concepts to clinically tested therapies. Future progress will depend on identifying the optimal patient population, product format and delivery route, reducing the need for immunosuppression, and demonstrating meaningful improvements in patient hospitalization, quality of life, and survival.

papers.title: Complementary Hydrogen-Bonded Dual-Network Bismaleimides for Cohesive Adhesion at Metal–Polymer Interfaces
papers.abstract: Abstract Herein, we present a strategy for designing thermally stable adhesive compositions that synergistically balance hydrogen-bond-mediated interfacial adhesion with network-derived bulk cohesion. Complementary hydrogen bonding between carbazole- and benzophenone-based bismaleimides (BMIs) establishes a cohesive molecular framework, while 2,2′-diallylbisphenol A (DABPA)-mediated allyl–maleimide ene reactions regulate network evolution to alleviate brittleness and improve processability. Subsequent incorporation of low-viscosity epoxy prepolymer promotes substrate wetting and generates hydroxyl functionalities during curing while yielding an interpenetrating polymer network. Nonisothermal differential scanning calorimetry analyses of the BMI compositions revealed pseudo-first-order curing behavior, and kinetic modeling demonstrated composition-dependent curing kinetics that govern curing reactivity and melt processability. With the subsequent incorporation of 30 phr of epoxy prepolymer, BMI–DABPA exhibited a low melt viscosity of 0.019 Pa·s, providing sufficient fluidity for resin spreading and substrate wetting. The resulting complementary hydrogen-bonded dual-network BMI adhesive delivered a lap shear strength of 11.53 MPa on an Fe substrate while maintaining excellent thermal stability (Td5% > 407 °C; char yield >43% at 800 °C). This work demonstrates the potential of balancing adhesion, cohesion, and processing characteristics in BMI adhesives by designing a reactive monomer system of sufficiently low viscosity, providing a rational molecular design strategy for future developments.

papers.title: Advances in electrode materials and interfacial chemistry of lithium-ion-based energy storage devices
papers.abstract: Recently, lithium-ion capacitors (LICs) have emerged as a new energy-storage technology that combines the characteristics of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) and supercapacitors. Their development has been driven by the growing demand for electrified transportation, stationary grid-storage systems, and portable electronic devices. In this review, recent advances in electrode materials and electrolyte chemistry, as well as interfacial phenomena for performance evaluation of LIBs and LICs, are discussed. Various carbon anodes and cathodes, transition metal oxides, phosphates, and chalcogenide-layered materials, as well as aqueous, nonaqueous, solid-state, and gel-polymer electrolytes used in LIBs and LICs are reviewed. Performance comparisons among electrode materials and full cells are presented, and the limitations of using metal electrodes, as well as strategies to improve them, are evaluated. The kinetic trade-off between the battery anode and the capacitor cathode, the balancing of electrode mass ratios, and the SEI/CEI interphases under high-voltage and high-rate regimes are considered in detail, along with recycling technologies and environmentally friendly synthesis routes for biomass-based electrode materials. Through systematic comparison of materials, mechanisms, performance, and degradation pathways, this review offers a practical approach to screening suitable electrode-electrolyte pairs for safer, more durable, and higher-performing future LIBs and LICs.

papers.title: Cellulose Nanocrystal‐Reinforced Polyurethane Foams From Sawdust Liquefaction Using Crude Glycerol and Polyethylene Glycol
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Rigid polyurethane (PU) nanocomposite foams were prepared from a sawdust‐derived polyol obtained by liquefaction with crude glycerol (CG) and polyethylene glycol (PEG) and reinforced with cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) at 0, 1, 3, and 5 wt% relative to polyol mass. CNC morphology was examined by atomic force microscopy (AFM), while foam morphology, chemical structure, thermal stability, density, compressive strength, and thermal conductivity were evaluated by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), density measurements, compression testing, and thermal conductivity analysis. Increasing CNC content decreased the average cell diameter from 170 to 80 μm. Foam density increased from 0.071 to 0.093 g cm −3 , while compressive strength enhanced from 0.275 to 0.410 MPa. The density‐normalized compressive strength promoted from 3.87 to 4.41 MPa (g cm −3 ) −1 , indicating that the mechanical improvement was not attributable to density alone. In addition, the degradation temperature increased and thermal conductivity decreased from 0.034 to 0.022 W m −1 K −1 . The FTIR spectra confirmed the successful formation of urethane linkages during the polymerization process. The results demonstrated the potential of CNCs to improve the performance of bio‐based polyurethane foams containing sawdust‐derived polyols.

papers.title: Microwave‐Assisted Synthesis of Fly Ash/Bamboo Leaf Ash‐Based Geopolymer for Methylene‐Blue Adsorption
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Despite its significant economic contribution, the textile industry remains a major source of dye pollution due to extensive untreated wastewater discharge. This study introduced a facile microwave–assisted strategy for converting fly ash (FA) and bamboo leaf ash (BLA) into value‐added porous geopolymer composites for the adsorption of methylene blue (MB) from aqueous solutions. By systematically varying the FA/BLA ratio, it reveals how BLA incorporation governs composite properties and organic‐dye removal performance. As the BLA content increased from 0% (100FA) to 60% (40FA60BLA) in the geopolymer composition, both the BET surface area and BJH pore volume increased significantly. The sample 100FA showed a surface area of 24.4 m 2 /g and a pore volume of 0.019 cm 3 /g, whereas 40FA60BLA reached 54.6 m 2 /g and 0.045 cm 3 /g, respectively. The high silica content in BLA facilitated the formation of smaller pores in the geopolymer network, fitting the Langmuir isotherm model and achieving a maximum MB‐adsorption capacity of 26.6 mg/g. Moreover, these geopolymers with the addition of BLA still gained above 50% of removal percentage of MB molecules after five consecutive cycles. Moreover, the incorporation of BLA also enhanced the treatment of real textile wastewater compared to those of FA geopolymer. These findings suggested that the incorporation of BLA into FA‐based geopolymers provided an effective and sustainable strategy for dye removal in wastewater treatment while promoting the valorization of industrial by‐product and agricultural waste.

papers.title: Multifunctional composite magnetic particles combined with static magnetic field for treating infectious bone defects via SLC2A1-mediated HIF-1 and PI3K/AKT pathways
papers.abstract: Abstract Infectious bone defects are a major challenge in orthopedics and stomatology, requiring strategies that eliminate bacteria and promote osteogenesis. Here, we developed a multifunctional composite magnetic particle system (F-Fe 3 O 4 ) and demonstrate its synergistic combination with a static magnetic field (SMF) for treating infectious bone defects. In vitro, F-Fe 3 O 4 demonstrated good biocompatibility with human bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (hBMSCs) and facilitated their proliferation, migration, and osteogenic differentiation, while inhibiting the growth of Escherichia coli , Staphylococcus aureus , and Enterococcus faecalis . With the application with SMF, the aforementioned effects are further enhanced. The in vivo studies in the rat model further revealed that F-Fe 3 O 4 combined with SMF can reduce early infection, alleviate inflammation, and accelerate new bone formation. Mechanistically, RNA sequencing and verification experiments revealed that the combination therapy upregulated SLC2A1 -mediated glucose uptake and activated HIF-1 and PI3K/AKT signaling pathways, thereby enhancing the osteogenic differentiation of hBMSCs. In conclusion, this study developed an efficient treatment approach for infectious bone defects by integrating F-Fe 3 O 4 and SMF.

papers.title: Efficient deoxygenation of palm oil to green diesel using a metal oxide catalysts supporting on ZrO2-enhanced graphene oxide
papers.journal: Universiti Putra Malaysia Institutional Repository (Universiti Putra Malaysia)
papers.abstract: NiO, Fe2O3, and bimetallic oxide NiFe2O4 catalysts supported on graphene oxide and promoted with ZrO2 were synthesized via wet-impregnation approach. A systematic characterization of the catalysts physicochemical properties was evaluated using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR), Temperature-programmed desorption CO2 (TPD-CO2), Brunaur-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area, Field emission Scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), and Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) analysis. The catalysts were evaluated as heterogeneous catalysts in the deoxygenation (DO) of palm oil for green diesel production under varying operating conditions. Among the catalysts tested, Fe2O3/ZrO2-GO (calcined at 400 °C for 4 h, 5 wt% loading) demonstrated superior catalytic activity, achieving a maximum hydrocarbon yield (HC%) of 98.0%, bio-jet fuel (BJF) selectivity of 40%, and kerosene yield of 86%. The exceptional performance is attributed to the catalyst’s large BET surface area (18.64 m2/g), substantial pore volume (0.027 cm3 /g), and moderate surface basicity (3234.65 μmol/g), which collectively facilitate efficient deoxygenation via decarboxylation (DCO2) and decarbonylation (DCO) pathways while suppressing undesired cracking. Furthermore, the catalyst exhibited remarkable stability and reusability over four consecutive reaction cycles, retaining 92% hydrocarbon yield and 80.9% kerosene yield, with BJF selectivity increasing to 84%. The gradual decline in performance is attributed to carbon deposition (coke formation), pore blockage, and sintering-induced degradation of the mesoporous network, as confirmed by post-reaction XRD and BET analysis.

papers.title: Detecting the onset and progression of spinodal decomposition using transient grating spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Abstract Spinodal decomposition can degrade corrosion resistance and embrittle materials. The ability to quickly, non-destructively detect spinodal decomposition via elastic property measurements before catastrophic materials degradation would represent a significant advance in materials testing. We demonstrate that spinodal decomposition can be detected in a binary Fe-Cr alloy via modulus stiffening using ex situ (and in situ) transient grating spectroscopy (TGS). The modulus stiffening is attributable to the convex dependence of the $$C{\prime}$$ C ′ elastic modulus on chromium content within certain compositional limits, which has been established by prior density functional theory studies. Over this range of initial chromium compositions, chromium partitioning due to spinodal decomposition raises the average $$C{\prime}$$ C ′ modulus such that the decomposed Fe-Cr alloy is stiffer than the initial solid solution. The presence and extent of spinodal decomposition in a 36 at. % chromium alloy are confirmed using atom probe tomography (APT), and are consistent with atomistic simulations that predict elastic modulus stiffening in the same alloy. The observed spinodal decomposition via APT is used to predict an expected modulus stiffening which, based on a simple model, agrees in sign and order of magnitude with the observed stiffening via TGS. The quantitative link between an observed composition change and a measured elastic response suggests TGS as a potential tool for non-destructive evaluation of spinodal decomposition in high-chromium ferritic phases in steels.

papers.title: Statistical Design of Thermal Protection System Using Physics-Informed Neural Network
papers.journal: ASCE-ASME Journal of Risk and Uncertainty in Engineering Systems Part B Mechanical Engineering
papers.abstract: Abstract Thermal protection systems of space vehicles are designed computationally rather than experimentally. They are validated using ground experiments, but all aspects of the flight cannot be replicated on ground. This ground-to-flight mapping introduces uncertainties which need to be accounted for while designing any thermal protection system. Thus, precise computational models along with uncertainty quantification in the models are required to design the TPS. The focus of this study is to estimate the thermal material parameters of TPS based on the target reliability requirements using statistical methods. To perform uncertainty quantification of a system, a simulated model of the system needs to be solved many times on statistical samples, increasing the computational time and cost of the overall process. In this study, a physics-informed neural network model is used in the analysis instead of traditional physics-based numerical solutions. The accuracy of PINN is comparable to that of the numerical solution. To find the parameter distribution, sampling of the parameter space is performed using Sequential Monte-Carlo method. The sampling method is efficient as it generates samples based on the target distribution in parallel. The framework can approximate the parameter distributions that satisfy the TPS design reliability constraints. The framework achieved a remarkable increase in the speed; specifically, the time required to process 10,000 samples was reduced 175 times using the proposed PINN-SMC. This reliability analysis can be used for design optimization of the TPS based on risk analysis along with other systems of the vehicle.
papers.summary: Abstract Thermal protection systems of space vehicles are designed computationally rather than experimentally. The focus of this study is to estimate the thermal material parameters of TPS based on the target reliability requirements using statistical methods. To find the parameter distribution, sampling of the parameter space is performed using Sequential Monte-Carlo method.

papers.title: Plasma and CSF neurofilament light chain measured by Simoa and Lumipulse: an inter-platform comparison across neurological disorders
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction Blood neurofilament light chain (NfL) is an accessible biomarker of neuroaxonal injury across a broad range of neurological disorders, but its clinical implementation requires robust cross-platform analytical and clinical comparability. The objective of this study was to evaluate the analytical and clinical comparability of plasma NfL measurements using Simoa and Lumipulse across different neurological conditions, by assessing cross-platform agreement and the ability of both assays to distinguish neurological diseases from healthy controls. Paired CSF analyses were performed in a subset of participants to biologically anchor plasma findings to the central compartment. Methods 383 individuals were included, comprising healthy controls and patients with neurodegenerative conditions, multiple sclerosis and stroke. Plasma NfL was measured in all participants using both Simoa and Lumipulse, with paired CSF analyses in a subset of 92 individuals. The Lumipulse testing intermediate precision and between-day repeatability was assessed as by the CLSI EP15. Cross-platform agreement for plasma NfL was evaluated using correlation analyses, Passing–Bablok regression and Bland–Altman analysis. Associations between plasma/CSF NfL concentrations were assessed using Spearman’s rank correlation analysis for each platform, separately. Age-adjusted cross-diagnostic differences were evaluated using permutation ANCOVA and multiple linear regression models for each platform, separately. Results Plasma NfL measured by Simoa and Lumipulse showed strong cross-platform concordance in the whole cohort (ρ=0.90), with similarly strong concordance observed for CSF NfL in the subset with paired samples (ρ=0.90). Method-comparison analyses in plasma demonstrated consistent agreement between platforms, with identifiable constant and proportional bias, alongside systematically higher absolute plasma NfL values measured by Lumipulse. Within-platform analyses showed significant correlations between plasma and CSF NfL concentrations (ρ=0.72 for Simoa; ρ=0.78 for Lumipulse). Noteworthy, Lumipulse NfL CSF and Blood kits exhibited high precision and analytical accuracy. Across both assays, plasma NfL increased with age and was significantly elevated in patients with neurological disorders compared with healthy controls. Discussion Simoa and Lumipulse capture a consistent biological signal in plasma across patients with neurological disorders, although their absolute NfL values differ, supporting the use of platform-specific reference ranges in clinical practice.

papers.title: dictyBase 2026: a reimplementation of the Dictyostelium model organism database on minimal infrastructure
papers.abstract: Dictyostelium discoideum is a model organism used to investigate a wide array of biological processes including chemotaxis, cell motility, phagocytosis, multicellular development, and autophagy. Many of its genes have human orthologs implicated in disease, making it a useful model organism for studying conditions ranging from cancer to neurodegeneration. dictyBase has served this community for two decades as a home for genomic data, protocols, a stock center, and community news. Here we describe a complete reimplementation of dictyBase as a self-contained service that uses static data files rather than a database server. Each gene record gathers curated function, human-disease context, developmental expression, and protein structure in a single webpage. The site also provides tools for sequence search, genome browsing, enrichment analysis, and experimental design. The complete Dicty Stock Center catalog of 7055 strains and 1265 plasmids is included, and both can be ordered from the site. New literature is curated by an author-in-the-loop pipeline. A language model drafts the annotations, the authors of the paper correct them, and a curator approves them. Analyses can be run on curator-approved annotations alone or extended to include those still awaiting review. dictyBase is freely available at https://dicty.org.
papers.summary: Dictyostelium discoideum is a model organism used to investigate a wide array of biological processes including chemotaxis, cell motility, phagocytosis, multicellular development, and autophagy. Each gene record gathers curated function, human-disease context, developmental expression, and protein structure in a single webpage. dictyBase is freely available at https://dicty.org.

papers.title: PROSWIN: Probabilistic Solar Wind Speed Forecasting Using Deep Distributional Regression From Solar Images
papers.abstract: Abstract Accurately predicting fast solar wind conditions is challenging, as uncertainties are large and unquantified by traditional single‐value prediction models. In particular, the risks of high‐speed solar wind streams (HSSs), which can cause damage to technological infrastructure, cannot be reliably assessed without probabilistic forecasts. We present PROSWIN, a probabilistic machine learning model that forecasts the hourly solar wind speed (SWS) at Earth with a 4‐day lead time. The approach combines solar images and magnetograms using a deep neural network coupled to a distributional regression algorithm. Because standard error metrics underweight the relevance of HSS peaks, we further introduce the prediction score (PS) , a model‐selection metric that jointly rewards timeline and HSS peak accuracy. On 14 years of data, our forecast achieves very well‐calibrated uncertainties (<1% average absolute coverage deviation). Using the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), a metric that assesses distributional accuracy, we obtain a timeline CRPS of 41.0 km/s, an HSS peak CRPS of 45.3 km/s, and a PS of 42.3 km/s. We find that the 171 Å channel is an important complement to the typically used 193 and 211 Å channels and that the PS for model selection improves the applicability of the model. Compared to selected models from the literature, ours is the only one that is accurate for both timeline and HSS peak values, rather than trading one off against the other. These results support the advantages of probabilistic over single‐value solar wind models. The introduced methods are also transferable to other forecasting problems.

These results support the advantages of probabilistic over single‐value solar wind models. The introduced methods are also transferable to other forecasting problems.
