papers.title: Development and Pharmacokinetic Evaluation of Drug-Loaded Mucoadhesive Microsphere For Enhanced Oral Bioavailability in Peptic Ulcer Management
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The present study aimed to develop and evaluate Vonoprazan Fumarate-loaded mucoadhesive microspheres for sustained drug release and improved oral drug delivery in the management of peptic ulcer disease. The microspheres were prepared using the ionotropic gelation technique, employing sodium alginate as the primary polymer, chitosan as the mucoadhesive polymer, and calcium chloride as the cross-linking agent. The prepared formulations (F1–F5) were evaluated for percentage yield, particle size, drug entrapment efficiency, mucoadhesion, swelling index, surface morphology, in-vitro drug release, drug–excipient compatibility, and stability. Among the formulations, F4 was selected as the optimized formulation based on its overall formulation characteristics. F4 exhibited a percentage yield of 91.18 ± 0.94%, drug entrapment efficiency of 88.63 ± 1.12%, mucoadhesion of 93.18 ± 1.04%, and a swelling index of 172.94 ± 4.11%. The in-vitro drug release study demonstrated sustained drug release, reaching 88.64% at 24 hours. Differential scanning calorimetry indicated no significant drug–excipient incompatibility under the investigated conditions. During accelerated stability testing at 40 ± 2°C/75 ± 5% relative humidity for two months, the optimized formulation showed minimal changes in drug content and drug release. In the in-vivo evaluation, F4 demonstrated promising gastroprotective activity, with an ulcer index of 1.28 ± 0.12, ulcer protection of 85.19%, and gastric pH of 3.94 ± 0.16. The reported pharmacokinetic findings also indicated increased systemic exposure compared with the conventional drug suspension; however, numerical pharmacokinetic data are required for quantitative confirmation. Overall, the findings suggest that Vonoprazan Fumarate-loaded mucoadhesive microspheres may offer a promising approach for sustained drug release and gastroprotective delivery in peptic ulcer management. Further studies with complete pharmacokinetic data are necessary to confirm the improvement in oral bioavailability.

papers.title: Efficacy and safety of novel non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists in diabetic kidney disease: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
papers.abstract: Aims To evaluate the efficacy and safety of novel non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (nsMRAs) in diabetic kidney disease (DKD). Methods Following PRISMA 2020, we searched four databases to 31 July 2026, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing nsMRAs with placebo in adults with DKD. Pooled estimates used random-effects models, with mean differences (MDs) for continuous outcomes and odds ratios (ORs) for dichotomous outcomes, each with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Risk of bias was assessed with Cochrane RoB 2, and certainty of evidence with GRADE. Results Eight RCTs (15,143 patients) were included. nsMRAs reduced log-transformed UACR (MD -0.36 log mg/g, 95% CI -0.44 to −0.28; n = 14,512 from 8 trials, predominantly driven by finerenone (5 of 8 trials), with significant drug-type interaction; P < 0.00001) and systolic BP (MD -4.72 mmHg, 95% CI -8.64 to −0.80; n = 7,538 from 3 trials (6 trials reported systolic BP; only 3 were poolable); predominantly driven by FIGARO-DKD; P = 0.02), but increased serum potassium (MD 0.22 mmol/L, 95% CI 0.16 to 0.29; n = 1,468 from 4 trials (6 trials reported serum potassium; FIDELIO-DKD and FIGARO-DKD excluded); P < 0.00001) and induced early eGFR decline (MD -3.01 mL/min/1.73 m 2 , 95% CI -4.46 to −1.56; n = 1,218 from 3 trials; P < 0.0001). Hyperkalemia risk was higher (OR 2.24, 95% CI 1.99 to 2.52; n = 14,734 from 6 trials; P < 0.00001), whereas overall adverse events, eGFR decline, and acute kidney injury did not differ. GRADE certainty was low for UACR, systolic BP, serum potassium, and early eGFR decline, and moderate for hyperkalemia. Conclusion In DKD, nsMRAs may reduce UACR and systolic BP. However, UACR was driven by finerenone with significant drug-type interaction, requiring agent-specific interpretation. Systolic BP was driven by FIGARO-DKD. Furthermore, nsMRAs may increase serum potassium and hyperkalemia risk, although the serum potassium analysis excluded two large trials. nsMRAs may also cause early hemodynamic eGFR decline. Notably, this review assessed only surrogate endpoints and safety outcomes. Several outcomes were supported by only 3–4 trials. Given these limitations and low-to-moderate certainty, findings warrant cautious interpretation and risk-benefit assessment. Systematic Review Registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251072300 , identifier CRD420251072300.

papers.title: Bioinspired Hydroxyapatite-Mineralized Silk Fibroin/Ionic Liquid Interpenetrating Hydrogels for Biomedical Applications
papers.abstract: Abstract Surgical site infection remains a critical barrier to successful bone tissue engineering, and silk fibroin (SF)-based scaffolds, despite their excellent biocompatibility, lack intrinsic antibacterial activity. Here, we report a multifunctional biohybrid nanocomposite hydrogel that integrates methacrylated silk fibroin (SFMA) with an antibacterial imidazolium-based ionic liquid monomer, 1-vinyl-3-hexylimidazolium bromide ([C6VIm]Br), fabricated via a bioinspired bidirectional freeze-casting strategy followed by in situ biomineralization with hydroxyapatite (HAp). Successful methacrylation (degree of substitution = 35%) and ionic liquid synthesis were confirmed by NMR spectroscopy, while FT-IR, TGA/DTG, and XRD analyses verified the formation of the interpenetrating SF/IL network and progressive HAp deposition, with mineral content rising from 12.1 to 32.9 wt % over successive mineralization cycles. SEM imaging and elemental mapping revealed a highly interconnected, anisotropic porous architecture with uniform calcium/phosphorus distribution, closely emulating native bone microstructure, and mineralization enhanced the swelling capacity to approximately 170%. Biologically, the ionic liquid component conferred potent, additive-free antibacterial activity against both Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli, while HAp incorporation improved MG-63 osteoblast-like cell adhesion and the viability of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs), with MSC viability exceeding 120% of the control in the mineralized sample. All formulations exhibited hemolysis well below accepted safety limits, confirming excellent hemocompatibility. By combining intrinsic antibacterial function, bioinspired anisotropic architecture, and biomimetic mineralization within a single platform, this work offers a promising, metal- and antibiotic-free strategy for infection-resistant scaffolds for bone tissue engineering, with significant potential for advancing bone tissue engineering and regenerative medicine.

papers.title: Family physicians’ acceptability, perceived value, and barriers of pharmacist-led medication management in primary care—a theory-based qualitative study
papers.abstract: Background Polypharmacy burdens healthcare systems and increases adverse drug events. While pharmacist-led comprehensive medication management (CMM) mitigates these issues globally, its integration into Turkish primary care remains limited. Objective To explore family physicians’ acceptability of pharmacist-led CMM in Türkiye and identify perceived barriers to interprofessional collaboration. Methods A qualitative descriptive study was conducted among primary care family physicians in Istanbul, Türkiye, between June and August 2025. Purposive sampling was utilized to recruit participants with at least 5 years of clinical experience. We collected data through semi-structured online interviews using a guide developed by an interdisciplinary panel and piloted for structural clarity. With NVivo software, transcripts were analyzed using a hybrid thematic analysis approach, combining inductive coding to identify emergent, context-specific themes with deductive mapping to the seven constructs of the Theoretical Framework of Acceptability (TFA). Inter-coder reliability was established through independent parallel coding, and trustworthiness was reinforced via member checking. Reporting adhered to the COREQ checklist. Results Participants ( n = 12) facing severe daily workloads (>74 patients) viewed clinical pharmacists as a crucial safety net. Analysis revealed three core themes: (1) Needs and Opportunities: CMM offers substantial benefits by managing polypharmacy, mitigating physician fatigue, reinforcing patient medication adherence, and reducing overall workload and costs. (2) Concerns and Barriers: Major structural hurdles include physical space constraints in FHCs, data privacy (KVKK) vulnerabilities, and pharmaceutical industry apprehension. (3) Implementation Conditions: Successful integration requires integrated Electronic Health Records (EHR), formalized legal boundaries, and joint interprofessional training. Subgroup analysis indicated that early- to mid-career physicians demonstrated higher implementation readiness, while late-career peers focused more on operational burdens. Conclusion Family physicians demonstrate highly favorable prospective acceptability toward pharmacist-led CMM. Successful real-world integration requires resolving macro-level infrastructural and legal barriers while establishing actionable interprofessional enablers, shared clinical algorithms, and compatible digital workflows.

papers.title: Low‐Outgassing Liquid Metal–Silicone Composites for Multifunctional Space Applications
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Space‐grade elastomers provide critical sealing, adhesion, and damping functions in spacecraft but require low outgassing to avoid contamination of sensitive optical and electronic components. Silicone elastomers are widely adopted due to their environmental stability, mechanical reliability, and ease of processing. Here, we introduce a multifunctional, low‐outgassing liquid metal elastomer composite with a space‐grade silicone matrix (S‐LMEC) that combines the mechanical reliability of the silicone with enhanced thermal and electrical properties. Dispersed LM microdroplets enable a 2.3 higher breaking strain, an 11 increase in thermal conductivity, and a 9.6 increase in dielectric permittivity without hindering curing. Thermogravimetric analysis demonstrates that the embedded LM does not compromise the underlying thermal stability of the polymer matrix while active electronic testing indicates the S‐LMEC significantly lowers the steady‐state temperatures by promoting rapid heat dissipation. Furthermore, the material can be patterned into complex structures via direct ink write 3D printing. The outgassing evaluation of the S‐LMEC indicates a total mass loss (TML) of 1.00%. To demonstrate practical utility, the S‐LMEC was integrated into a wearable capacitive tactile glove for soft robotic skin applications. This materials platform expands the design space for space‐grade elastomers, enabling advancements in planetary exploration soft robotics and on‐demand electronics manufacturing.

papers.title: DSC-CAN: a cross-attention network with dual-space calibration for RF-based open-set UAV identification
papers.abstract: Abstract The rapid expansion of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) applications increases the demand for reliable low-altitude airspace monitoring. Radio-frequency (RF)-based UAV identification provides a passive and non-visual solution by exploiting transmitter-dependent signal characteristics. In open-world deployments, an RF monitoring system needs to recognize known UAV emitters while rejecting previously unseen RF signals. However, open-world RF monitoring remains challenging because known UAV signals often exhibit substantial intra-class variations, while unseen signals can lie close to known-class distributions. These factors make it difficult to preserve known-class discrimination and reliably reject unknown signals under resource-constrained deployments. To address these limitations, we propose the Dual-Space Calibrated Cross-Attention Network (DSC-CAN), a parameter-efficient framework for open-set RF UAV identification. We first employ a compact local–global cross-attention encoder to coordinate fine-grained RF patterns and long-range contextual dependencies, thereby learning compact and discriminative representations. We then introduce class-adaptive prototype-radius calibration to construct class-specific acceptance regions from known training and calibration data, enabling adaptive boundary estimation without using unknown test samples. Finally, we develop dual-space geometric fusion to combine Euclidean prototype-distance evidence with contrastive cosine evidence, thereby suppressing unreliable acceptance decisions when the two spaces provide inconsistent support for a known class. Experiments on multiple known–unknown class partitions show that DSC-CAN achieves strong and stable open-set performance with only 0.187 M parameters. In the primary scenario, DSC-CAN obtains an H -score of 0.9542, an AUROC of 0.9847, an FPR@95 of 0.0368, and an OSCR of 0.9586. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of the overall design and the complementary roles of its components.

papers.title: Population-level spatial patterns of body-surface temperature in older adults: a multicenter infrared thermography study across diverse environmental settings
papers.abstract: Background Body-surface temperature reflects peripheral physiological regulation and may provide a useful phenotype for population studies of ageing. Infrared thermography (IRT) enables non-invasive assessment of temperature distribution, but large multicenter evidence remains limited. We aimed to characterise body-surface temperature patterns in older adults and examine their associations with individual and contextual factors. Methods In this multicenter observational study, 5,225 adults aged ≥60 years underwent standardized IRT across multiple regions in China. Temperature was measured at 12 predefined trunk regions. Both absolute regional temperature and plane-specific relative temperature (ΔT) were analyzed. Multivariable regression models adjusted for demographic, anthropometric, physiological, and center-related variables were used to assess constitution-by-region interactions, followed by false discovery rate-adjusted region-specific analysis. Sensitivity analysis included absolute-temperature models and leave-one-site-out validation. Results A total of 62,700 region-level observations were analyzed. Regional setting was the largest contributor to thermal variability, followed by body composition, whereas constitution explained a relatively small proportion of overall variance (2.0–10.9%). Significant constitution-by-region interactions indicated spatially heterogeneous temperature patterns (χ²=732.41, df=88, p<0.001). Constitution-related differences were localized mainly to abdominal, posterior lumbar, and selected thoracic regions, with modest effect sizes (0.08–0.27 °C) that remained directionally consistent across sensitivity analysis. Conclusion Body-surface temperature in older adults exhibits modest but spatially organized variation influenced predominantly by regional setting and body composition. Constitution-related differences are localized and reproducible but should be interpreted as exploratory surface-temperature phenotypes rather than clinically actionable findings.

papers.title: A conserved EREG+IL1RN+ macrophage program defines an inflammation-associated transcriptional state linked to WTAP reprogramming and preterm premature rupture of membranes
papers.journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
papers.abstract: Preterm premature rupture of membranes (PPROM) is a major cause of spontaneous preterm birth, yet the cellular mechanisms linking inflammation to membrane dysfunction remain incompletely understood. Here, we integrated single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomic datasets from multiple maternal-fetal interface tissues to construct a comprehensive atlas of inflammatory signaling during early pregnancy. Macrophages emerged as the predominant source of basal inflammatory activity, and secondary clustering identified a conserved EREG + IL1RN + macrophages characterized by elevated inflammatory and innate immune programs. Pseudotime analysis revealed a transcriptional progression from proliferative and immunoregulatory macrophage states toward inflammatory and immune-effector states, with EREG + IL1RN + macrophages exhibiting a distinct transcriptional profile. Independent single-nucleus and spatial transcriptomic datasets confirmed the transcriptional and spatial conservation of this population. In placental infection datasets, EREG + IL1RN + macrophages were markedly expanded and enriched for cytokine signaling, leukocyte recruitment, and extracellular matrix remodeling pathways. WTAP , an m 6 A-associated candidate regulator, was positively associated with inflammatory macrophage programs, and its depletion attenuated inflammatory gene expression while promoting immunity hub-associated signatures. Clinically, the EREG + IL1RN + macrophage signature was significantly enriched in PPROM fetal membranes and showed the strongest ability to distinguish PPROM from preterm labor controls. Together, these findings identify EREG + IL1RN + macrophages as a conserved inflammatory macrophage program and implicate WTAP in inflammatory macrophage remodeling at the maternal-fetal interface.

papers.title: Sustainable Self-Healing Thermoresponsive Nanocomposite Derived from Shrimp Shells and Lignin Biowaste for Water Shutoff in Ultradeep High-Temperature, High-Salinity Carbonate Reservoirs
papers.abstract: Abstract Excessive water production in ultradeep, extreme high-temperature and high-salinity (HTHS) carbonate reservoirs has emerged as a major challenge, reducing hydrocarbon productivity and creating substantial environmental and economic burdens. Herein, we report, for the first time, the synthesis of a novel, highly resilient, sustainable, self-healing, thermoresponsive chitin-based nanocomposite hydrogel for water shutoff, specifically tailored to endure extreme harsh conditions of 160 °C and 350,000 ppm salinity. The nanocomposite was synthesized via a near-zero-waste approach utilizing chitin and CaCO3 nanoparticles derived from shrimp shell biomass, employing a recyclable, CO2-switchable natural deep eutectic solvent (NADES)-assisted enzymatic process. The extracted chitin was copolymerized with vinyl ester sulfonated lignin (VESL), a green macromonomer derived from industrial lignin waste, and 1-vinylimidazole (VIm) via free radical polymerization. The hydrogel composition has been optimized using response surface methodology (RSM) with central composite design. The nanocomposite was thoroughly characterized by FTIR, 1H NMR, SEM, EDX, TGA, and DTG analysis. The optimized nanocomposite demonstrated a superior swelling ratio and viscoelastic properties even at an ultralow polymer concentration of 0.08 wt % across temperatures of 25 to 160 °C and salinities up to 350,000 ppm. Core-flooding experiments indicated effective fracture plugging with high RRF values of 300.5 ± 5.7 and 191.1 ± 4.8 (with plugging efficiencies of 99.7 ± 0.4% and 99.5 ± 0.5%, respectively) using ultralow nanocomposite concentrations of 0.08 wt % and 0.1 wt %, respectively. This research presents a sustainable strategy that integrates the CO2-switchable green extraction of chitin with lignin for valorization of marine and industrial biowaste into a high-performance self-healing hydrogel for water shutoff in ultra-HTHS reservoirs.

papers.title: Separated thermal–mechanical damage modelling of concrete at elevated temperatures: formulation, ABAQUS implementation, and fire performance prediction
papers.abstract: Predicting the response of concrete to fire remains difficult because of the complex, coupled thermal and mechanical damage that develops at elevated temperatures, which existing constitutive models often treat in a lumped or inconsistent manner. This study develops a thermodynamically consistent damage–plasticity model in which thermal and mechanical damage evolve through independent, energy-based laws, coupled with temperature-dependent plasticity and a full strain decomposition that includes thermal expansion and transient creep. The model is implemented as an ABAQUS UMAT subroutine to enable analysis from the material to the structural scale. Model predictions were validated against published experimental data over the range 20–600 °C. At the material scale, the predicted compressive strength decreases from 39 MPa at ambient temperature to 30 MPa (77%) at 400 °C and 14 MPa (36%) at 600 °C, while the thermal damage variable reaches 0.36 and 0.75, respectively. At the structural scale, the predicted peak capacity of reinforced concrete beams decreases from 470 to 360 and 175 kN over the same range, consistent with test data. A fire-protection design study further shows that, for the specific column geometry and loading condition analysed, a 20 mm coating provides the most favourable balance between capacity retention and material cost for achieving an R120 rating. The proposed framework offers a physically based tool for assessing the high-temperature performance of concrete.

papers.title: Near-infrared responsive theranostic platforms: toxicological challenges, biological interactions, and clinical translation
papers.abstract: The disease microenvironment is a complex milieu containing unique biochemical and biophysical cues, such as acidosis, oxidative stress, hypoxia, enzymatic imbalance, and microorganisms, which influence not only the effectiveness of treatments but also the fate and safety of the nanomedicine. NIR-responsive dyes and dye-conjugated nanomaterials have attracted considerable attention for diagnostic and therapeutic applications owing to their deep tissue penetration, external-stimulus activation, and precise spatiotemporal control. Despite notable progress in developing NIR-responsive systems for cancer, inflammatory diseases, and infections, their clinical use is limited by issues such as toxicity, degradation, biodistribution, accumulation, persistence, and immune reactions to nanomaterials. Importantly, recent studies have shown that the disease microenvironment can significantly affect the degradation, activation, bioactivity, and toxicity of NIR-responsive systems, yet these issues remain scattered in the literature. Specific attention is paid to structure–toxicity relationships, phototoxicity, immunotoxicity, biodegradability, biodistribution, organ-specific accumulation, and long-term safety, as well as emerging contrasts between NIR-I and NIR-II-based systems. We additionally elaborate on advanced experimental models, regulatory approaches, and safety and design approaches, such as biodegradable systems, renal-clearance-based systems, and smart activated nanomaterials.

papers.title: Thermal Stability and Environmental Degradation of YB 2 C 2 Ceramics
papers.journal: Journal of the American Ceramic Society
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates the melting, oxidation, and ambient moisture‐induced corrosion behaviors of high‐purity yttrium borocarbide (YB 2 C 2 ) ceramics. The YB 2 C 2 ceramic exhibited decomposition and melting behaviors at approximately 2100°C under low‐vacuum conditions (below 20 Pa). Thermogravimetric (TG) analysis performed between 40°C and 1400°C in air, combined with x‐ray diffraction (XRD) analysis, confirmed that the significant oxidation of sintered YB 2 C 2 initiates above 810°C. This process leads to the extensive phase transformation into YBO 3 , B 2 O 3 , and Y 2 O 3 after the thermal cycle. Furthermore, the sintered YB 2 C 2 was observed to react with atmospheric moisture under ambient conditions, disintegrating into a fine powder while forming amorphous yttrium and boron hydroxide species. The resulting morphology and crystalline structure of these hydro‐corroded products differed significantly from those of the oxidation products. The underlying mechanisms for the oxidation and ambient moisture corrosion were systematically analyzed. These findings indicate that YB 2 C 2 ceramics may require robust environmental barrier coatings (EBCs) or other protective strategies for practical applications in oxygen‐ or moisture‐containing environments.

papers.title: Herbal Fast-Dissolving Oral Films: Bridging Phytotherapy and Innovative Drug Delivery
authors: Mukta M. Lande, Neha G. Mohite, Nikita R. Ingle
Kanchan M. Tejankar Maitreyi R. Shinde
Dr.K. R. Biyani Prof. S. D. Sagrule
papers.journal: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
papers.abstract: Fast-dissolving oral films (FDOFs), also known as oral thin films (OTFs) or mouth-dissolving films (MDFs), are innovative drug delivery systems designed to dissolve or disintegrate rapidly in the oral cavity without the need for water. These thin polymeric films offer advantages such as ease of administration, portability, improved patient convenience, and suitability for paediatric, geriatric, and dysphagic patients. Herbal fast-dissolving oral films have gained research interest as a potential approach for incorporating plant extracts and phytoconstituents into convenient oral dosage forms. They are generally formulated using natural or synthetic film-forming polymers, plasticizers, sweeteners, flavouring agents, and other suitable excipients. Various manufacturing techniques, including solvent casting and hot-melt extrusion, may be employed depending on the properties of the herbal ingredients and formulation components. The quality and performance of these films are assessed using parameters such as thickness, weight variation, folding endurance, surface pH, content uniformity, mechanical strength, disintegration time, drug release, and stability. Depending on the formulation and absorption pathway, the released constituents may produce local effects or undergo systemic absorption. However, improved bioavailability and therapeutic efficacy must be established experimentally. This review discusses the formulation components, polymer selection, manufacturing methods, packaging materials, evaluation parameters, advantages, limitations, and potential applications of herbal fast-dissolving oral films in pharmaceutical drug delivery.

papers.title: Numerical Investigation of Post-Earthquake Fire Resistance of Reinforced Concrete Column
papers.journal: International Journal of Inventive Engineering and Sciences
papers.abstract: Post-earthquake fire (PEF) is a critical multi-hazard scenario that can cause severe structural degradation and collapse, even in buildings designed for modern seismic and fire codes. This study conducts a comprehensive numerical investigation of a reinforced concrete columns behaviour under seismic lateral loading and post-earthquake fire loading. We developed a validated 3D finite element (FE) model in ANSYS Mechanical to simulate coupled thermal–mechanical behaviour, incorporating nonlinear concrete damage, reinforcement yielding, and heat-dependent material properties. Experimental results reported in the literature were used for validation analyses using FEA tools such as ANSYS, and a comprehensive parametric study was subsequently carried out to examine the influence of axial load ratio (0.1–0.4), concrete cover thickness (25–50 mm), and number of fire-exposed faces (one, three, four) on PEF resistance. Results show that higher axial load ratios significantly reduce ductility and fire resistance, while more fireexposed surfaces accelerate reinforcement heating and stiffness degradation. Thicker concrete cover improves thermal protection but can reduce lateral resistance by reducing effective depth. Finite element validation results showed good agreement with experimental residual lateral load capacity, with margins of error of 4.7 parcent and 2.2 parcent for lateral load capacity and ductility ratio, respectively. Concrete cover size influenced insulation efficiency and residual strength. Compared with 35, 40, and 50mm concrete cover, a nominal 25mm concrete cover showed a 3.2 parcent, 19.1 parcent, and 59.63 parcent increase in rebar reinforcement temperature. Postearthquake fire (PEF) peak lateral load capacity and fire resistance also decreased by 8.1 parcent compared with seismic lateral loading alone. The findings highlight critical design-sensitive parameters governing PEF resistance and emphasise the need for integrated multi-hazard design approaches in structural engineering practice.

Results show that higher axial load ratios significantly reduce ductility and fire resistance, while more fireexposed surfaces accelerate reinforcement heating and stiffness degradation. papers.title: Spatio-temporal dynamics and driving factors of the Production–Ecological–Living Spaces in the Funiu Mountain Area from 2000 to 2020
papers.abstract: Introduction Scientific understanding of the spatio-temporal evolution of Production-Ecological-Living Spaces (PELS) and their driving factors provides theoretical support and practical guidance for territorial spatial planning. This study aimed to investigate the spatio-temporal evolution of PELS and explore its driving factors in the Funiu Mountain area. Methods Digital elevation models (DEMs), multi-source datasets of natural, social, and economic driving factors, and the geographical detector method were used to analyze the spatio-temporal evolution of PELS and identify its driving factors. Results From 2000 to 2020, the area of production space showed a shrinking trend, whereas the areas of ecological space and living space expanded. Among these, grassland ecological space and urban living space expanded significantly. Across different elevation zones, production space decreased in area. Ecological space increased slightly in low-altitude areas (<400 m), while changes in medium- and high-altitude areas were relatively stable. Living space increased across all elevation zones. Urban living space and industrial production space underwent the most frequent changes. In terms of spatial transformation, exchanges between ecological space and production space were dominant, followed by those between living space and production space, whereas transformations between ecological space and living space were infrequent. The evolution of PELS was primarily influenced by natural background conditions, while the driving effects of socio-economic factors became increasingly prominent. The q value of economic density increased 26.4-fold (from 0.0064 to 0.1688), while that of population density increased 7.5-fold, highlighting the increasingly important role of socio-economic factors in shaping the spatial pattern. Discussion Unlike existing regional-scale investigations, this study identifies the elevation-gradient differentiation of the driving mechanisms underlying PELS evolution in mountainous areas. These findings enrich the theoretical understanding of PELS in mountain regions and provide targeted support for territorial spatial optimization and sustainable, coordinated regional development in the Funiu Mountain area.

papers.title: The FaesMYB15-FaesELF3 module regulates flowering time, floral organ number, and floral color in red flower long-homostyle common buckwheat
papers.abstract: EARLY FLOWERING 3 (ELF3) is a core member of the Evening Complex (EC) and plays a critical role in regulating flowering through the plant circadian clock. R2R3-MYB transcription factors (TFs) control the transcriptional regulation of anthocyanin structural genes involved in anthocyanin accumulation in various plants and also play important roles involved in floral development. However, how ELF3 homologs work together with R2R3-MYB TFs to regulate flowering, floral organ development, and flower color remains unclear. In this study, R2R3-MYB TF FaesMYB15 directly binds to the FaesELF3 promoter and suppresses expression of FaesELF3 in common buckwheat. In addition, overexpression of FaesELF3 in red flower LH Fagopyrum esculentum leads to significantly earlier flowering and rapid plant growth, and results in flowers with increased tepal and stamen numbers and a lighter tepal color in transgenic plant. Moreover, total anthocyanin content in the inflorescence of the 35S::FaesELF3 line was significantly lower than that of the normal red flower LH common buckwheat. FaesELF3 overexpression markedly downregulated the expressions of two core circadian clock genes, FaesPRR5–1 and FaesPRR5-2 , and two AGAMOUS -like MADS-box genes, FaesAGL18 and FaesAGL19 , involved in flowering regulation in transgenic plants. Our study introduces a new regulator module of FaesMYB15-FaesELF3 involved in regulating flowering time, floral color, and floral organ number in crops, providing insights for novel breeding strategies of flowering regulation and flower color modification in common buckwheat.

papers.title: Technical note: Machine learning metamodelling for global sensitivity analysis
papers.abstract: Abstract. Global sensitivity analysis (GSA) plays a central role in hydrologic modelling by supporting model understanding, diagnosis, and decision-making through the identification of influential and non-influential parameters and their interactions. Variance-based methods provide a rigorous framework for GSA but are often computationally expensive, as their estimation requires a large number of model evaluations. Metamodelling has therefore been widely adopted as a strategy to alleviate this issue, with recent advances in machine learning (ML) offering new opportunities to construct accurate and flexible surrogates for complex models. This technical note examines the practical relationship between Sobol’ total-effect indices (Ti) and feature importance measures derived from ML metamodels within a hydrologic modelling context. Building on theoretical results that link Ti to permutation variable importance (PVIi) under independence assumptions, we provide systematic numerical evidence using three conceptual hydrologic models of varying complexity (HBV, HyMod, and VIC) applied to three headwater catchments in northern Germany, together with three ML metamodels: a random forest (RF), a neural network (NN), and a linear model (LM). The three metamodels were trained on Monte Carlo samples and used to estimate sensitivities through PVIi and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAPi). The results demonstrate that RF and NN metamodels reliably reproduce both the ranking and relative magnitude of Ti using PVIi across all hydrologic models, providing clear empirical support for the theoretical connection between the two measures. In contrast, the performance of LM-based estimates depends strongly on the degree of linearity in the underlying model response. Mean absolute SHAPi values exhibit a consistent monotonic relationship with Ti and preserve parameter rankings, while sample-specific SHAPi values enable a distributed evaluation of sensitivities across both the parameter space and the target variable space. Overall, this study highlights ML metamodelling as a computationally efficient and conceptually sound framework for GSA in hydrologic modelling and beyond.

The results demonstrate that RF and NN metamodels reliably reproduce both the ranking and relative magnitude of Ti using PVIi across all hydrologic models, providing clear empirical support for the theoretical connection between the two measures. In contrast, the performance of LM-based estimates depends strongly on the degree of linearity in the underlying model response.

papers.title: Urban-to-downwind variations in aerosol composition and optical properties in the Paris urban plume from coordinated airborne and ground-based observations
papers.abstract: Abstract. Aerosols play a critical role in Earth’s climate, but substantial evolution in their physicochemical properties after emission introduces uncertainties in predicting their climate impacts. Observational constraints on how aging modifies aerosol properties remain limited. Here, we investigate the effects of ~2–6 h of aging on aerosol physicochemical properties using coordinated airborne and ground-based measurements in Paris and its downwind regions. Urban plumes contributed modestly to particle number concentrations in the 80–200 nm size range and resulted in a moderate enhancement of submicron particle (PM1) mass relative to out-plume background levels. Organic aerosol (Org) dominated PM1 mass both near the urban source and downwind. Aircraft observations showed enhanced Org and non-refractory PM1 relative to excess CO (CO above surrounding background) in downwind plumes, indicating net secondary organic aerosol production during aging. Aerosol optical properties evolved concurrently. Downwind plume-average single-scattering albedo (SSA) at 450 and 630 nm was higher than near-source values. Consistently, the complex refractive index shifted from lower real (~1.35–1.40) and higher imaginary (~0.03–0.08) components near source to higher real (~1.45–1.50) and lower imaginary (~0.015–0.02) components downwind. The absorption Ångström exponent also increased, indicating a greater fractional contribution of brown carbon to light absorption. These results demonstrate that urban plume aging alters aerosol composition and optical properties and highlight the need to represent evolving aerosol characteristics in atmospheric models and remote-sensing retrievals.

Aircraft observations showed enhanced Org and non-refractory PM1 relative to excess CO (CO above surrounding background) in downwind plumes, indicating net secondary organic aerosol production during aging. These results demonstrate that urban plume aging alters aerosol composition and optical properties and highlight the need to represent evolving aerosol characteristics in atmospheric models and remote-sensing retrievals.

papers.title: Quantitative Pathway-Resolved Kinetics from Neural Network-Guided Weighted Ensemble Simulations
papers.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.abstract: Abstract Many crucial biomolecular processes, such as ligand dissociation and conformational switching, occur via multiple competing transition pathways. While standard rare-event sampling methodologies provide rigorous estimates of the global transition rate, they typically collapse the underlying mechanistic heterogeneity into a single global constant, obscuring the relative kinetic contributions of distinct channels. Here, we introduce a path-resolved weighted ensemble (WE) framework that quantitatively assigns steady-state flux to competing transition channels without modifying the underlying unbiased dynamics. In our approach, initial reactive trajectories generated via direction-guided adaptive sampling are clustered by dynamic time warping (DTW) and smoothed into neural-network-refined representative paths. These refined routes are formulated as path collective variables (PathCVs) to preseed and guide channel-specific WE simulations. We demonstrate the robustness of this framework across systems of increasing complexity. On a model three-hole potential, the method accurately captures a temperature-dependent pathway crossover. In the benzamidine–trypsin complex, it isolates the dominant unbinding route while quantifying the fluxes of subdominant channels. Finally, for imatinib dissociation from Abl kinase, the method reveals that the clinically relevant N368S resistance mutation drastically redistributes reactive flux from the P-loop/hinge channel toward the αC-helix channel, accelerating escape. This framework successfully translates qualitative pathway classification into rigorous, pathway-specific kinetic observables, offering a powerful tool for understanding mutation-induced mechanistic shifts in biomolecular function.

papers.title: Synthesis-by-design of ferroelectric Dion–Jacobson two-dimensional hybrid organic–inorganic perovskites
papers.abstract: Abstract Dion–Jacobson two-dimensional hybrid organic–inorganic perovskites are promising ferroelectric materials, combining chemically tunable polarity enabled by their organic spacers with enhanced environmental stability. However, rational discovery remains difficult owing to uncertain phase formability and scarce, biased ferroelectric data. Here we show a staged, physically guided synthesis-by-design workflow that integrates learning from scarce ferroelectric data with structure-aware screening. Starting from 11 known ferroelectric compounds in this family, symbolic regression defines a descriptor-bounded ferroelectric-consistent region. Similarity-guided expansion and chemical filtering reduce 83,924 molecules to 1012 candidate divalent spacers, while machine-learned interatomic-potential relaxation and connectivity analysis identify 338 candidates retaining Dion–Jacobson connectivity. Sequential prioritization by connectivity retention, chemical similarity, energetic refinement and synthetic accessibility selects s −2-fluorobutane-1,4-diamine, leading to the synthesis of a PbI 4 -based Dion–Jacobson perovskite with experimentally confirmed ferroelectric switching. This prospective proof of concept shows how sparse property knowledge can be coupled with structural screening to prioritize organic spacer candidates for experimental synthesis.

papers.title: Building AI (In)dependence through EU’s AI Factories
papers.abstract: This paper analyses the European Union’s flagship initiative to become an international leader in AI: the 19 AI Factories, spread across 16 EU Member States. At the moment, a few large AI companies from the US (‘Big AI’) hold key parts of the AI market. Smaller European startups therefore struggle with barriers to entry, lock-in effects, and dependencies in the global ‘AI race’. The AI Factories try to respond to this – but to what extent can they achieve their high ambitions? By employing a doctrinal analysis of the relevant EU law and semi-structured interviews with nine industry experts (six AI startup representatives, two Big AI representatives, and one AIF representative), the study analyses the capacity of the AI Factories to function as public alternatives to Big AI. Our findings indicate that while the AI Factories – on paper – offer free access for startups to AI-optimised supercomputing, technical support, data services, and regulatory guidance, their real-world impact remains limited at this time. This is mainly due to limited awareness among startups, misalignment with startups’ commercialisation needs, and restrictions that limit AI Factory use to model training rather than deployment. Furthermore, the platform lock-in to Big AI further reduces startups’ willingness to ‘migrate’ and train their models with the AI Factories. The paper concludes that, as of now, the AI Factories alone are unlikely to reduce startups’ reliance on Big AI, but combined with stronger competition enforcement and targeted industrial policy, they could contribute to a more self-reliant European AI system.

papers.title: Acidification and Nutritional Changes During Controlled Fermentation of Bambusa spinosa Roxb. Shoots Using Indigenous Lactic Acid Bacteria
papers.abstract: This study evaluated two indigenous lactic acid bacteria isolates as starter cultures for controlled fermentation of Bambusa spinosa Roxb. shoots. BSISO1 and BSISO14, recovered from fresh B. spinosa Roxb. shoots, were selected based on colony morphology and Gram stain reaction. Based on 16S rRNA gene sequencing, the isolates were putatively identified as Lactiplantibacillus plantarum BSISO1 and Lactiplantibacillus pentosus BSISO14. Three fermentation treatments were established: BSISO1-inoculated, BSISO14-inoculated, and uninoculated spontaneous fermentation. The inoculated treatments received 3% (v/v) starter culture and were fermented for 14 days. The pH and total titratable acidity (TTA) were monitored every two days, while fat, reducing sugar, protein, and crude fiber were measured at the end of fermentation. Treatment, fermentation day, and their interaction significantly affected acidification. BSISO1 produced the lowest overall pH and highest overall TTA, followed by BSISO14, while spontaneous fermentation showed the weakest acidification. Fermentation markedly reduced reducing sugar and crude fiber relative to fresh shoots, whereas fat remained relatively stable. BSISO14 showed numerically higher protein and crude fiber values than spontaneous fermentation. These results indicate preliminary potential that BSISO1 and BSISO14 can support controlled fermentation of B. spinosa shoots, with BSISO1 showing stronger acidification performance. Further microbial, metabolomic, sensory, safety, and shelf-life evaluations are required before practical starter-culture application.
papers.summary: This study evaluated two indigenous lactic acid bacteria isolates as starter cultures for controlled fermentation of Bambusa spinosa Roxb. These results indicate preliminary potential that BSISO1 and BSISO14 can support controlled fermentation of B. spinosa shoots, with BSISO1 showing stronger acidification performance.

papers.title: Tuning ferroptosis-like, cancer-selective cell death with charge-imbalanced nanoparticles
papers.abstract: Abstract It is known that nanoparticles functionalized with mixed charge monolayers – that is, monolayers composed of both positively [+] and negatively [-] charged ligands – can induce selective death of cancer cells. Remarkably, however, when the ligand polarities and proportions are kept constant, but the chemical nature of the “minority” [-] component is altered, the nanoparticles exhibit distinct intracellular localization patterns and induce different forms of iron-dependent lipid-peroxidation-driven cell death, which we term “ferroptosis-like” due to concurrent activation of caspases. In particular, changing the end groups on the [-] ligands from carboxylic to sulfonic to phosphonic acid shifts nanoparticle accumulation from lysosomes to autophagic compartments to late endosomes, respectively. These distinct cellular outcomes are accompanied by marked differences in the composition of serum protein coronas adsorbed onto the mixed-charge nanoparticles. Proteomic analysis revealed exceedingly complex corona proteomes, comprising more than 800 different proteins, many enriched hundreds- to thousands-fold compared to blood serum, with numerous proteins selectively enriched on specific nanoparticle types. Together, these findings identify charge-imbalanced constructs as potential modulators of subcellular organelle targeting and ferroptosis-like cell death.

papers.title: Combining enhanced basalt weathering with soda saline soil: A novel CO₂ mineralisation strategy
papers.abstract: Enhanced rock weathering in saline–alkaline soils can couple CO₂ mineralisation with reclamation of salt-affected land. We incubated 30 g basalt with 30 g sodic saline soil for 90 days at 15 °C using three particle sizes (0.074, 0.42 and 5 mm) and two water additions (30 and 60 g). Endpoint aqueous chemistry, SEM–EDS, thermogravimetric analysis and PHREEQC saturation modelling were integrated with a regional life-cycle assessment for Jilin Province, China. Endpoint Ca accounting yielded apparent weathered-basalt masses, which were converted using a primary Ca-only carbonate capacity of 0.072 g CO₂ g⁻¹ basalt and an all-base-cation carbonate-equivalent upper capacity of 0.142 g CO₂ g⁻¹ basalt. Particle-size-specific effective rates linked the incubation results to 30-year weathering trajectories. Gross CDR reached 72.45–72.47 kg CO₂ t⁻¹ basalt in the primary case and 141.92–141.96 kg CO₂ t⁻¹ basalt in the upper case. Across twelve scenarios, primary-case net CDR ranged from −5.53 to 38.45 kg CO₂-eq t⁻¹ basalt, while upper-case net CDR ranged from 63.96 to 107.92 kg CO₂-eq t⁻¹ basalt. Net-removal costs ranged from USD 1327–29,328 t⁻¹ CO₂ in the primary net-removing scenarios and from USD 473–4667 t⁻¹ CO₂ in the upper case. The identified 6376,490 ha of Jilin cropland, equivalent to 482.06 Mt basalt at 75.6 t ha⁻¹ , had gross capacities of 34.93 Mt CO₂ (primary) and 68.43 Mt CO₂ (upper). Finer particles reached the composition-controlled capacity sooner, whereas coarse basalt had lower supply-chain emissions in the evaluated scenarios.

papers.title: Synergistic catalytic co-pyrolysis of eucalyptus bark and polyethylene over natural clinoptilolite: Thermogravimetric and kinetic evidence
papers.abstract: Catalytic co-pyrolysis is a promising strategy for thermochemical conversion of biomass and plastic wastes; however, the combined influence of hydrogen-rich polymers and natural zeolite catalysts on reaction kinetics remains poorly understood. This study investigated the effects of low-density polyethylene (LDPE) and natural clinoptilolite (CLIN) on the thermal degradation behavior, interactions, and apparent activation energies of eucalyptus bark (EB). Thermogravimetric analyses were performed under pyrolysis, catalytic pyrolysis, co-pyrolysis, and catalytic co-pyrolysis conditions at 10, 30, and 50 K min −1 . Interactions were evaluated using the deviation method, while apparent activation energies were determined using the Friedman and Kissinger–Akahira–Sunose (KAS) methods. Co-pyrolysis with LDPE produced composition- and heating-rate-dependent synergistic and inhibitory interactions and reduced the mean apparent activation energies in the lignin/LDPE-dominated region relative to pure LDPE. Clinoptilolite modified the kinetic behavior depending on blend composition and catalyst loading. Catalytic co-pyrolysis of the blend containing 50 wt% LDPE and 15 wt% CLIN exhibited particularly low mean apparent activation energies in Regions I and II, and the highest pyrolysis performance index among catalytic blends at 50 K min −1 . These findings support the potential application of low-cost natural zeolites in biomass–plastic co-pyrolysis.

papers.title: Luminescent Iridium(III) Complex with Alkoxy-Functionalised 2-Phenylpyridine Ligands: Synthesis, Spectroscopic and Photophysical Studies
papers.abstract: Cyclometalated iridium(III) complexes have garnered considerable interest owing to their exceptional photophysical properties and broad applicability in luminescence-based technologies.This work describes the preparation, spectroscopic analysis, and photophysical characterisation of a new emissive iridium(III) complex, [Ir(bFppy)₂(eFppy)], incorporating the ligands 2-(2butoxy-4-fluorophenyl)pyridine (bFppy) and 2-(2-ethoxy-4-fluorophenyl)pyridine (eFppy).The structure identity of the complex was confirmed by ¹H NMR, ¹³C NMR, and FTIR spectroscopic techniques.In the ¹H NMR spectrum, aliphatic proton signals were observed between δ 1.00-4.09ppm, corresponding to the ethyl and butyl chain protons, while signals in the δ 5.99-8.81ppm region were attributed to aromatic protons of the phenylpyridine frameworks.A total of 43 carbon resonances were resolved in the ¹³C NMR spectrum, in complete accordance with the number of carbon atoms anticipated from the proposed structure.Complementary FTIR data supported these assignments through the observation of C-H, C=C, and C=N stretching bands characteristic of the complex.UV-Vis spectroscopy identified π-π* intraligand transitions in the ultraviolet region and MLCT transitions extending into the visible range.Steady-state emission measurements revealed that the complex produces intense green phosphorescence in dichloromethane solution at ambient temperature, with an emission maximum at λem = 502 nm, indicative of an emissive pathway dominated by ³MLCT character.The efficient triplet-state emission exhibited by this complex highlights its promising prospects for applications in optoelectronic devices, such as organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs).

papers.title: Hydraulic behavior and solute redistribution of saline-alkali black soil: Implications for stormwater source control
papers.abstract: Study Region Daqing, northeastern China, has saline-alkali soils, strong evaporation, and shallow groundwater that constrain infiltration-based stormwater source control. Study Focus We examined hydraulic behavior and water and solute redistribution in black soil amended with 0, 0.5, and 2.0% Na 2 CO 3 . Saturated hydraulic conductivity ( K s ) was measured after 0~4 wetting-drying cycles. Soil water retention was determined by the filter paper method, and unsaturated hydraulic conductivity ( K u ) was estimated with the van Genuchten-Mualem model. A complementary column experiment applied sequential rainfall depths of 10, 20, 40, and 70 mm to track soil moisture, electrical conductivity (EC), and gravel layer water EC. New Hydrological Insights for the Region: Na 2 CO 3 addition reduced initial Kₛ from 3.31 × 10 −6 m/s at 0% to 2.49 × 10 −7 and 3.02 × 10 −8 m/s at 0.5% and 2.0%. Wetting-drying caused further declines, while estimated Kᵤ remained lower in Na 2 CO 3 -amended soils over most of the modeled suction range. During sequential rainfall, the 2.0% treatment accumulated more water near the surface and responded more slowly at depth. EC decreased in the upper 20 cm but increased at 20~40 cm, while gravel layer water EC increased by only 8.9%. Low hydraulic conductivity therefore restricted vertical water transmission and promoted solute accumulation within the soil profile.

Soil water retention was determined by the filter paper method, and unsaturated hydraulic conductivity ( K u ) was estimated with the van Genuchten-Mualem model. Low hydraulic conductivity therefore restricted vertical water transmission and promoted solute accumulation within the soil profile.

papers.title: Synthesis and Characterization of New Additive, 4-(3-bromophenyl)thiosemicarbazide for High-Conductivity Polymer Electrolyte
papers.abstract: Thiosemicarbazides are valued for their biological activities and versatile applications, with nitrogen and sulfur donor atoms offering new potential in polymer electrolyte studies.The main goal of this research is to synthesize and characterize 4 -(3-bromophenyl) thiosemicarbazide and investigate its conductivity.4-(3-bromophenyl)thiosemicarbazide was prepared by reacting 3-bromophenyl isothiocyanate with hydrazine hydrate and was successfully synthesized in 89% yield.CHNS analysis confirmed its high purity with <1% deviation from theoretical values.FTIR (cm⁻¹): 3275, 3146 [ν(N-H)]; 1632 [δ(NH₂) + ν(C=C)ₐᵣ]; 1571 [ν(C=C)ₐᵣ]; 1524 [δ(N-H)]; 1211 [ν(C=S)]; 1076 [ν(C-N)]; 763 [γ(C-H)ₐᵣ]; 696 [ν(C-Br)].¹³C NMR displayed signals at 180 ppm (C=S) and 121-141 ppm (aromatic carbons), confirming the proposed structure.UV-Vis spectra showed absorption at 270 and 212 nm, assigned to π→π* and n→σ* transitions, respectively.Thermogravimetric analysis revealed a multi-step decomposition, indicating its thermal stability.Single-crystal XRD revealed a monoclinic crystal system (space group P2₁/n) with unit cell parameters a = 6.2948(4)Å, α = 90°; b = 28.1751(18)Å, β = 99.168(2)°;c = 10.8098(7)Å, γ = 90°, revealing intermolecular N-H••S and N-H••Br hydrogen bonds, and C-H••π and N-H••π interactions.The UV-Vis Tauc plot gave a band gap of 5.36 eV, while DFT calculated 4.92 eV, indicating a wide-band-gap electronic structure.EIS measurements indicated an ionic conductivity of 8.87 × 10⁻⁵ S cm⁻¹ at room temperature for the sample containing 10 wt% additive.Upon incorporation of 5 wt% 2,6-pyridinedicarboxylic acid, the conductivity increased by 8.3-fold to 7.32 × 10⁻⁴ S cm⁻¹ at room temperature, reaching a maximum of 8.60 × 10⁻⁴ S cm⁻¹ at 50 °C, beyond which thermal degradation effects reduce conductivity.Temperature-dependent studies revealed non-Arrhenius behavior, with conductivity peaking at 50°C (8.60 × 10⁻⁴ S cm⁻¹) and declining at higher temperatures, consistent with a negative apparent activation energy (Ea = -2.21kJ/mol) arising from thermal degradation effects that dominate above 50°C.Thus, the material shows great potential as a conductive additive for polymer electrolyte-based energy storage applications, with tunable ionic transport properties within its operational temperature window (<50°C).

papers.title: Comparative Physicochemical Characterization of Green Waste Compost Tea from Different Feedstocks
papers.abstract: Rising concern over environmental impacts of excessive agrochemical fertilizer use has drove to surge in interest of converting waste into compost and compost tea, a sustainable alternative offering diverse physicochemical and biological interactions.This study characterizes the physicochemical properties of non-aerated green waste compost tea prepared from anaerobically composted green waste such as bamboo shoot (BS), banana peels (BP), green vegetables (GV) and leaves of java ginger (JG), Curcuma xanthorrhiza.Physicochemical parameters (pH, EC, TDS, ORP, salinity), nutrient concentrations (ammonium nitrogen, phosphorus), and antioxidant activity (DPPH assay) were determined alongside elemental (C, H, N, S) and FT-IR analyses.Results revealed a significant variation among feedstocks.BP consistently exhibited the most favourable composition, with significantly higher nutrient content (ammonium nitrogen 0.33 mg/L; phosphorus 11.07 mmol/L), ionic strength (EC 16.58 mS/cm; TDS 8204 mg/L), phenolic concentration, and antioxidant activity (77% inhibition).In contrast, GV and JG teas showed comparatively lower nutrient and bioactive profiles.Elemental and FT-IR analyses confirmed the presence of carbohydrates, proteins and phenolics, underscoring the chemical diversity contributed by different green wastes.Collectively, these findings demonstrate that feedstocks selection strongly influences nutrient dynamics and antioxidant potential of compost tea.This study highlights dual function of compost tea as both a nutrient source and biostimulant, supporting its application as an eco-friendly agriculture input.

papers.title: Thermal consequences of fast–charging–induced anode aging in Lithium–Ion Batteries: Lifetime, safety, and modelling
papers.abstract: Fast charging improves battery availability, but the associated lifetime loss cannot be separated from the cell's changing thermal state. This review examines the effects of operating temperature, charge rate, state of charge, and accumulated resistance on heat generation, anode evolution, and thermal safety. The discussion focuses on the interaction between persistent solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) growth and rate–sensitive lithium plating. As SEI–related resistance develops, irreversible heating and anode polarization increase during later charging. Plated and dead lithium add reactive material that can bring forward self–heating. Cells at comparable states of health may consequently respond differently to thermal abuse when their aging histories produce different interphases, resistance distributions, and lithium inventories. Evidence from calorimetry, abuse testing, plating diagnostics, and electrochemical–thermal models is examined to identify the internal variables that can connect lifetime prediction with safety analysis. The resulting pathway–resolved view informs charging control and thermal–safety assessment, but also shows that SEI, plating, resistance, and spatial–temperature states must be transferred consistently between service and abuse models.

papers.title: Antibiotic and growth factor-loaded hydrogels for infected bone defect repair: mechanisms of spatiotemporal delivery and cellular microenvironment regulation
papers.journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
papers.abstract: The treatment of infected bone defects (IBDs) requires simultaneous infection control and bone regeneration. However, traditional staged treatment protocols have several limitations. These include extended treatment durations, multiple surgical procedures, and low repair efficiency. Bifunctional hydrogels loaded with antibiotics and growth factors (GFs) offer a crucial material platform for integrated treatment strategies. These hydrogels possess excellent biocompatibility, malleability, and the capacity for spatiotemporal drug delivery. This review summarizes the design principles of antibiotic- and GF-loaded hydrogels, with particular attention to sequential and synergistic release strategies and their roles in infection control, immune regulation, vascularization, and osteogenesis. Current in vitro and in vivo evaluation approaches are also discussed, together with remaining challenges in drug stability, release precision, long-term biosafety, and clinical translation. This review may provide a basis for the rational design of multifunctional hydrogel systems and their further development for infected bone defect repair.

papers.title: Cross-domain thermal-health prediction and early warning for lithium-ion batteries via dual-stream network
papers.abstract: The joint prediction of thermal states and State of Health (SOH) is vital to ensure the safe operation and reliable management of lithium-ion batteries. However, existing approaches usually model these targets independently. Such separate modeling leads to insufficient coupling awareness, restricts practical warning decision-making, and yields poor cross-domain generalization, which impedes reliable battery lifespan management. To tackle these challenges, this paper proposes a dual-stream multi-task network for joint thermal-health prediction and early warning to improve battery management systems. The architecture contains two parallel branches: a temporal convolutional network captures local thermal dynamics, while a Mamba model characterizes long-range degradation evolution. The outputs of the two branches are fed into adaptive gated fusion modules followed by task-specific prediction heads. An auxiliary temperature difference prediction task is introduced to improve thermal consistency, and a weighted loss function focusing on high-temperature regions is designed to enhance prediction reliability under safety-critical conditions. A domain distribution alignment strategy is further adopted to realize few-shot cross-environment domain adaptation. After alignment-based pre-training, a small number of labeled target-domain samples are utilized for model fine-tuning. Experiments under dynamic conditions on the XJTU dataset demonstrate that the proposed model achieves competitive performance, with a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.011 for SOH and 0.898 °C for maximum temperature. Cross-environment transfer tests on the NASA dataset obtain an SOH MAE of 0.022. Relying on the prediction results, the proposed warning scheme achieves a strict timely response rate of 92.6%, with an average warning lead time of 48.6 cycles across test cases. These results verify that the proposed framework enables proactive thermal-risk monitoring and holds great application potential for intelligent battery management.

These results verify that the proposed framework enables proactive thermal-risk monitoring and holds great application potential for intelligent battery management.

papers.title: Association between an improved positioning management strategy and non-incisional low back pain and sleep quality in patients undergoing modified radical mastectomy for breast cancer: a retrospective cohort study
papers.abstract: Background Non-incisional low back pain, particularly low back pain, and sleep disturbance are common yet underrecognized problems during early recovery after breast cancer surgery. This study evaluated whether an improved positioning management strategy was associated with reduced non-incisional low back pain and improved postoperative sleep quality. Methods This single-center retrospective cohort study included adult women who underwent modified radical mastectomy or simple mastectomy for breast cancer between January 2024 and December 2025. Patients were grouped according to whether an improved positioning management strategy was implemented during the perioperative period (intervention vs. control). Non-incisional low back pain was assessed using the Numerical Rating Scale (NRS, 0–10), and sleep quality was assessed using the Richards–Campbell Sleep Questionnaire (RCSQ: 0–100) at 24, 48, and 72 h postoperatively. Safety outcomes included total drainage volume during the first 3 postoperative days, subcutaneous seroma, and skin-flap ischemia or necrosis. Linear mixed-effects models with random intercepts were used for repeated measures, adjusting for age, body mass index (BMI), analgesic regimen, and postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV), with Holm correction for multiple comparisons. Gamma regression and Firth-penalized logistic regression were applied for safety outcomes. Results Baseline characteristics were generally comparable between groups, although BMI was slightly higher in the intervention group ( P = .04) and was adjusted for in multivariable analyses. Improved positioning management was associated with significantly lower non-incisional low back pain ( β = −0.711, P < .001). Pain increased over time in the control group, whereas significant group-by-time interactions indicated greater pain reduction in the intervention group at 48 h ( β = −0.358, P = .002) and 72 h ( β = −0.737, P < .001). Between-group differences in pain at all time points remained significant after Holm correction. The association remained significant after additional adjustment for incisional pain. Improved positioning management was also associated with higher postoperative sleep quality, with significant group and group-by-time effects at 24–72 h. No significant between-group differences were observed in drainage volume, seroma, or flap ischemia/necrosis. Conclusion An improved positioning management strategy was associated with reduced early postoperative non-incisional low back pain and better sleep quality after breast cancer surgery, without evidence of increased drainage- or flap-related complications. These findings should be interpreted as observational associations and warrant confirmation in prospective studies.

papers.title: Thermophysiological responses to occupational heat stress during simulated wildland firefighting in females and males: influence of fitness and body composition
papers.abstract: This study compared thermophysiological responses to prolonged exercise during prolonged occupational heat stress in female and male participants involved in wildland firefighting activities while wearing standard personal protective equipment. Twenty-two participants (11 females and 11 males) performed a graded exercise test followed by a prolonged submaximal protocol simulating wildfire suppression tasks in a controlled environment (30 °C, 30% relative humidity). Physiological responses, gastrointestinal temperature (T g ), chest skin temperature (T skin ), sweat production, and heat balance components were evaluated. Females exhibited higher mean values for most physiological variables, except rating of perceived exertion, which was higher in males. However, when responses were analyzed at matched relative exercise intensities, no meaningful sex-related differences were observed in T g , whereas chest T skin and heart rate remained higher in females. Body fat percentage was positively associated with T g and chest T skin ( r= 0.55 and 0.53), whereas VO 2max was negatively correlated with T g ( r= −0.47). This relationship disappeared when VO 2max was normalized to lean body mass. Heat dissipation pathways differed between groups: males showed greater evaporative heat loss, whereas females exhibited a greater contribution of dry heat exchange. These findings suggest that individual body composition and aerobic fitness may contribute to variability in thermophysiological strain during occupational uncompensable heat stress.

papers.title: Pemberdayaan Rumah Tangga Petani melalui Pengolahan Semangka Non-Grading menjadi Sirup Pasteurisasi di Kecamatan Pujut
papers.abstract: Semangka kategori *non-grading* sering kali memiliki nilai jual rendah karena tidak memenuhi standar pasar, meskipun sebenarnya masih layak dikonsumsi. Kegiatan pengabdian masyarakat ini bertujuan untuk meningkatkan pemahaman peserta mengenai pengolahan semangka *non-grading* menjadi sirop terpasteurisasi. Kegiatan dilaksanakan di Desa Segala Anyar, Kecamatan Pujut, Lombok Tengah, dengan melibatkan 15 peserta yang berasal dari keluarga petani dan Kelompok Tani Modern. Rangkaian kegiatan meliputi penyampaian materi, demonstrasi, praktik langsung, serta evaluasi melalui *pre-test* dan *post-test*. Evaluasi mencakup aspek pembuatan sirop, pasteurisasi, dan pengemasan. Skor rata-rata meningkat dari 2,55 pada *pre-test* menjadi 4,18 pada *post-test*, dengan kenaikan sebesar 1,63 poin. Peningkatan pemahaman tertinggi terjadi pada aspek pasteurisasi. Hasil kegiatan menunjukkan adanya peningkatan pemahaman peserta setelah pelatihan serta mengindikasikan bahwa kegiatan ini memberikan pengalaman praktis dalam mengolah semangka *non-grading* menjadi sirop terpasteurisasi.

papers.title: Epigenetic aging in the tumor microenvironment: mechanisms and implications for immunotherapy
papers.abstract: Aging reshapes the tumor microenvironment (TME) by altering the immune, stromal, and vascular compartments, yet these changes are not fully explained by chronological age. Epigenetic mechanisms, including DNA methylation, histone modifications, chromatin accessibility, and non-coding RNA programs, may contribute to persistent alterations in cellular function and communication. In this review, we synthesize current evidence on epigenetic remodeling in the aged TME, distinguishing established findings in aging and cancer from mechanisms that remain to be demonstrated specifically in aged tumors. We highlight how epigenetic changes intersect with cellular senescence, chronic inflammation, and metabolic stress to weaken antitumor immunity and influence treatment response, with particular attention to T-cell dysfunction, regulatory T-cells, myeloid cells, fibroblasts, and endothelial cells. We also discuss the limitations of bulk-tissue epigenetic clocks and the emerging value of cell-resolved and spatial analyses. Finally, we consider therapeutic implications, including epigenetic therapies, senescence-directed interventions, and selective targeting of suppressive immune-stromal interactions, while noting that their ability to reverse TME aging remains uncertain. Integrating longitudinal human studies with functional experiments will be essential to determine whether epigenetically altered immune-stromal niches can serve as biomarkers or therapeutic targets beyond chronological age alone.

papers.title: Sustainable Ammonium Metallates Enabling Efficient PET Waste Depolymerization
papers.abstract: Abstract The increasing volume and heterogeneity of post-consumer PET waste highlight the need for efficient and sustainable chemical recycling technologies capable of providing monomers of sufficient purity for closed-loop applications. In this work, we report a solvolytic process enabled by ammonium metallate catalysts, and in particular [TMA][FeCl4], designed to operate under less severe conditions than conventional depolymerization routes. The methodology employs methanol as the sole solvent at 170 °C, without acidic or basic additives, and affords DMT yields up to 90% at 1 mol % catalyst loading, while complete disappearance of insoluble PET is maintained even at loadings as low as 0.1 mol %. A systematic experimental plan, including catalyst screening, optimization, PET concentration effects, and mechanical-stirring assisted scale-up to 48 g of PET, demonstrates high robustness and excellent isolated yields across operating conditions. The process shows broad tolerance toward common polymeric contaminants and real post-consumer waste streams, including colored packaging and mixed textile substrates, yielding high-purity DMT after a single recrystallization. The recovered DMT was successfully reused for PET synthesis and further validated as a polyester-grade feedstock through the preparation of a PBT-based thermoplastic copolyester elastomer with properties comparable to appropriate benchmark materials. Overall, the less severe reaction conditions, low catalyst loading and cost, operational simplicity, waste-stream compatibility, and recovery of polymer-grade DMT highlight the potential of this approach for PET chemical recycling and monomer valorization.

papers.title: Environmentally Sustainable Chitin-Based Composite Structures Isolated from Lichens: Physicochemical Characterization and Biointerface Evaluation
papers.abstract: Lichens are complex symbiotic organisms composed of fungi and photosynthetic partners such as algae or cyanobacteria. While numerous bioactive compounds have been extracted from lichens, their insoluble, structural polymeric materials remain largely unexplored. In this study, the structural components of four lichen species—Xanthoparmelia pulla, Rhizoplaca chrysoleuca, Diploschistes scruposus, and Umbilicaria nylanderiana—were isolated through sequential demineralization, deproteinization, and decolorization processes to obtain sustainable biopolymeric matrices. The isolated materials were characterized using FTIR, XRD, TGA, SEM, and EDS analyses. The combined physicochemical analyses supported the presence of chitin-containing structural polysaccharides together with residual mineral components and revealed species-dependent differences in the chemical, crystalline, thermal, morphological, and elemental characteristics of the isolated materials. XRD analysis further revealed distinct diffraction profiles and contributions from residual crystalline mineral phases, particularly CaCO₃. SEM observations indicated species-dependent differences in surface morphology, while EDS confirmed the presence of C, N, O, Si, and Ca elements. The MTT assay revealed species-, concentration-, and time-dependent differences in L929 cell viability. Materials derived from X. pulla and R. chrysoleuca showed comparatively favorable cellular responses, whereas D. scruposus and U. nylanderiana caused significant reductions in cell viability. These findings provide comparative physicochemical and cellular-response data on lichen-derived structural materials and support their further investigation as naturally derived materials for potential biointerface applications.

papers.title: Double Vacancy CdS / Bi 19 Cl 3 S 27 Heterojunction with Inverted F‐Scheme and Internal Electric Field Constructed Via an Electrostatic Self‐Assembly Strategy for Boosted Photocatalytic Hydrogen Evolution
papers.abstract: Rationally designing heterojunction photocatalysts with directional charge transfer characteristics remains a challenge. Herein, we report a novel 0D/1D dual‐vacancy CdS/Bi 19 Cl 3 S 27 (denoted as CdS v /BCS v ) heterojunction photocatalyst with an inverted F‐scheme charge transfer mechanism via electrostatic self‐assembly. This unique charge transfer mechanism enables the optimized CdS v /BCS v ‐2 heterojunction to achieve a H 2 production rate of 446.8 μmol h −1 g −1 , which is 3.6 times higher than that of pure CdS v (123.3 μmol h −1 g −1 ) and 60.4 times higher than that of pure BCS v (7.4 μmol h −1 g −1 ). Mechanistic investigations, incorporating in situ characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, reveal that the enhanced activity originates from the formation of the CdS v /BCS v heterojunction, which promotes efficient photoelectron transfer from CdS v to BCS v . This work proposes an inverted F‐scheme charge transfer mechanism to enhance photocatalytic activity and provides a new strategy for constructing high performance dual‐defect composite photocatalysts for photocatalytic H 2 evolution.

papers.title: Extending a Thermal Runaway Modeling Framework to Cells of Different Formats, Sizes, and Chemistries
papers.abstract: Simplified staged thermal runaway (TR) models are attractive for early-stage battery safety assessment, but they are usually parameterized for a single cell type and rely on internal temperature measurements that are impractical in sealed cylindrical and pouch cells. This work extends a four-stage TR modeling framework so it can be applied to cylindrical and pouch cells of different sizes with nickel-rich layered-oxide cathodes using surface-temperature data from accelerating rate calorimetry (ARC) alone. Four modifications are introduced: an objective segmentation of the temperature-rate curve by three-segment piecewise regression with free breakpoints; a regularized extraction of the Arrhenius parameters that removes the ill-conditioned data at each stage end; a stage-dependent mass-loss function, including a two-step venting formulation for cells with delayed vent opening; and format-specific non-adiabatic boundary conditions for the severe and cooling phases. Adiabatic TR experiments were performed on three samples each of a 4.5 Ah 21700 NMC cylindrical cell, a 33 Ah 4695 NCMA cylindrical cell, and a 65 Ah NMC pouch cell. The model reproduces the measured temperature and temperature-rise rate for all three formats. The results quantify how strongly cell format governs TR severity and indicate that TR in large-format pouch cells can be accurately described without internal instrumentation. Applicability to prismatic cells and to other cathode chemistries, such as LFP, has not been demonstrated.

papers.title: A Porous Polymer of Thienothiophene and Tetraphenylethylene: Design, Synthesis and Photophysical Properties
papers.abstract: A novel conjugated porous polymer (CPP) based on thieno[3,2-b]thiophene (TT) and tetraphenylethylene (TPE) was successfully designed and synthesized via a Pd(0)-catalyzed Suzuki cross-coupling reaction. Owing to its rigid, highly cross-linked architecture, the resulting TT–TPE polymer is insoluble and exhibits permanent porosity. Comprehensive characterization using UV–Vis, fluorescence, and FTIR spectroscopy, together with scanning electron microscopy (SEM), cyclic voltammetry (CV), and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), confirmed the successful formation of a robust π-conjugated porous network. The polymer exhibits a strong π–π* absorption band at 392 nm, intense fluorescence emission at 549 nm, and a large Stokes shift, indicating efficient intramolecular energy transfer and significant excited-state relaxation. SEM images reveal a hierarchically porous, sponge-like morphology, while electrochemical studies demonstrate stable redox behavior and favorable HOMO and LUMO energy levels, highlighting its potential for optoelectronic applications. Furthermore, the optical and electrochemical band gaps are in good agreement, indicating the reliability of the experimental results. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further corroborate the experimental findings, showing excellent agreement between the simulated and observed electronic transitions. Overall, the TT–TPE conjugated porous polymer represents a promising functional material for applications in chemical sensing, energy storage, and optoelectronic devices.
