papers.title: Synergistic effects of fibrolytic enzymes and lactic acid bacteria on cassava leaf silage quality and microbial community
papers.abstract: Cassava leaves are a valuable protein-rich feed resource, but their high fiber content and poor fermentation characteristics can reduce silage quality. To address these challenges, this study evaluated the synergistic effects of fiber-degrading enzymes and lactic acid bacteria (LAB) on the fermentation profiles, nutritional quality, and microbial community of cassava leaf silage. Silage was prepared using five treatments: CK (2% glucose), T1 (Lactobacillus plantarum + 2% glucose), T2 (glucanase + L. plantarum + 2% glucose), T3 (cellulase + L. plantarum + 2% glucose), and T4 (glucanase + cellulase + L. plantarum + 2% glucose), and ensiled for 0, 21, and 42 days. The findings demonstrated that additive treatments (T1-T4) rapidly decreased silage pH and increased lactic acid compared to the CK (P < 0.001). By day 42, the enzyme-inoculated groups (T2-T4) exhibited elevated crude protein alongside reduced fiber fractions compared to both CK and T1 (P < 0.001). Regarding the microbial community, Shannon and Simpson indices were lower in treated groups than in the CK group (P < 0.05). Beta diversity analysis revealed that the microbial community structure of the CK differed clearly from that of the additive-treated silages. At the phylum level, Bacillota dominated all other groups on day 42, with a relative abundance exceeding 92%. At the species level, Lactobacillus plantarum dominated enzyme-treated silages (relative abundance > 93%, P = 0.036), compared to only 13.1% in CK, which contained higher proportions of Pediococcus and Weissella species. Collectively, the synergistic application of fibrolytic enzymes and LAB improves cassava leaf silage quality by accelerating acidification, reducing fiber fractions, and establishing a highly favorable L. plantarum-dominated microbial community.

papers.title: Floating 3D‐Printed Grids: New Approach for Photocatalytic Degradation of Contaminants Under Direct Solar Radiation
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Water contamination by antibiotics and other emerging contaminants is ubiquitous across all water matrices worldwide, and underlines the need for sustainable, easy‐to‐deploy materials that operate efficiently in real aquatic environments. A straightforward implementation is essential for bridging laboratory developments to diverse practical water‐treatment scenarios. In this work, floating poly(vinylidene fluoride‐co‐hexafluoropropylene) (PVDF‐HFP) grids incorporating TiO 2 were fabricated via direct ink writing (DIW) 3D printing combined with salt leaching, thereby enabling precise control over geometry and porosity while overcoming the structural limitations of conventional techniques. The resulting grids exhibited interconnected porosity, strong mechanical stability, remarkable reusability, and effective photocatalytic performance, achieving 60% degradation of ciprofloxacin in 540 min under UV‐A radiation and complete degradation in about 120 min under natural sunlight. Distinctively, the materials maintained their photocatalytic activity across multiple reuse cycles, demonstrating robustness and operational durability. These results highlight the potential of this 3D‐printed floating system to provide a scalable, customisable and practical solution for water remediation using just sunlight.

papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pain control in neonates is crucial as inadequate management may impair neuronal development. Dexmedetomidine (DEX), an alpha2 agonist, is approved for intravenous use in ventilated neonates. While intranasal DEX is off-label in neonates and children, studies show its efficacy for magnetic resonance imaging sedation. The method's suitability was verified by comparing results from nine paediatric blood samples collected in EDTA tubes or using MITRA devices. RESULTS: > 0.99), intra and inter-day repeatability (CV % 1.8-11.8), stability, and hematocrit effect met the acceptance criteria for bioanalytical method validation. Compared with plasma samples, the proposed method showed good consistency in detecting DEX in MITRA samples. CONCLUSION: The MITRA microsampling tools reduce the amount of blood needed and the risks of anemisation for neonates hospitalised and simplifies procedures, allowing a reduction of the staff involved in the routine. The analytical and clinical validation of the method demonstrated its suitability to quantify DEX in a range of concentrations potentially useful for pharmacokinetic studies in paediatric patients for approval use and drug monitoring.

papers.title: Agro-Waste Upcycling in Wound Care: Development And Characterization of An Alkali-Treated Coconut Coir and Alginate Composite Gauze for Sustained Herbal Delivery
authors: Ashwini G. Narwade, Ashwini K. Bhusari, Snehal R. Suradkar
Vaishnavi V. Shende Vaishnavi A. Deshmukh
Dr. S. L. Khedekar Dr. R. H. Kale
papers.journal: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
papers.abstract: Chronic and acute wounds place a heavy burden on patients and health systems, and conventional woven cotton gauze, although inexpensive and widely used, can adhere to the wound bed, shed lint and allow desiccation. Modern moisture-retentive dressings solve many of these problems but are costly and often non-biodegradable. At the same time, coconut (Cocos nucifera L.) processing generates very large quantities of husk that are burned or discarded. Coir, the lignocellulosic fibre of the husk, is porous, absorbent and biodegradable, and its properties can be improved by alkali and oxidative (H2O2) treatment. Sodium alginate, a seaweed polysaccharide that gels by ionic exchange with calcium, can be coated on a fibre matrix to create a moist, non-adherent, exudate-managing surface and a reservoir for herbal actives such as turmeric (Curcuma longa),neem, aloe vera and Centella asiatica. This review summarizes wound-healing physiology, the types of dressings, the history and limitations of gauze, the potential of agro-waste coir, the role of alginate hydrogels, and the evidence for herbal wound therapies. It then outlines a plan for developing and characterizing an alkali-treated coconut coir and alginate composite gauze for sustained herbal delivery, and identifies gaps that future work must address.

papers.title: Spatial and Spectral Decoupled Meta‐Window for Thermal Camouflage and Infrared Communication
papers.abstract: Thermal radiation carries energy and information, making simultaneous control of its spectral profile and spatial propagation crucial for infrared camouflage, signaling, and communication. However, most thermal materials prioritize spectral manipulation, leaving the propagation direction of broadband thermal signals underexplored and tightly coupled to the spectral response. Here, a spatial and spectral decoupled meta-window (SSDW) is demonstrated for independent control of the spectral profile and spatial distribution of broadband thermal radiation across 8-13 µm. By assigning directional reflection splitting and spectral tailoring to distinct geometric degrees of freedom, the SSDW exhibits visible haze, mid-infrared semitransparency, and broadband suppression of specular reflection, including at 10.6 µm. It maintains a stable apparent thermal signature both without external heat interference and under variations in external-source temperature, source incidence angle, and camera viewing angle. This enables visible-laser-infrared compatible camouflage, while preserving an outward channel for emergency signaling. As a proof-of-concept, the SSDW encodes the incidence direction of a 10.6 µm laser into spatial reflection patterns for assistive infrared communication, enabling reliable decoding over moderate angular variations. This work establishes spatial and spectral decoupling as a framework for thermal radiation engineering, extending control beyond radiative intensity toward coordinated heat and information pathways.

papers.title: Structural compatibility between β‐lactams and substrate binding pockets of IMP ‐1 and NDM ‐1 determines the substrate spectrum
papers.journal: Bulletin of the Korean Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Abstract The global spread of infectious diseases is exacerbated by rising antimicrobial resistance, with Metallo‐β‐lactamases (MBLs) contributing significantly by inactivating β‐lactam antibiotics. The enzyme's substrate spectrum is usually determined by structural compatibility between the substrate‐binding pocket (SBP) and the substrate. We studied the structural compatibility between the SBPs of IMP‐1 and NDM‐1 and six β‐lactam substrates, and the correlation between compatibility and hydrolytic activity. MBLs have a conserved SBP surrounded by three external loops. The SBP contains catalytic zinc‐binding sites at the center and R α and R β pockets on both sides. IMP‐1 has narrower R α and wider‐open R β pockets, while NDM‐1 has broader R α and less‐open R β pockets. Different classes of β‐lactams show distinct structural characteristics in the core rings and both side chains. We performed enzyme kinetics and molecular docking studies. Results show that higher structural compatibility, especially in the tighter R α pocket, is important for hydrolytic activity. The structural compatibility study will help clarify the substrate‐spectrum profile of MBLs across diverse β‐lactams.

Different classes of β‐lactams show distinct structural characteristics in the core rings and both side chains. Results show that higher structural compatibility, especially in the tighter R α pocket, is important for hydrolytic activity.

papers.title: Development and Evaluation of a Polymer-Based Topical Emulgel of Luliconazole for Effective Management of Superficial Fungal Infections Especially Tinea Pedis
papers.journal: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)
papers.abstract: Background: Luliconazole is a strong topical imidazole antifungal with poor water solubility that may limit medication availability from traditional formulations. The objective of the present work was to create and analyze a polymeric luliconazole emulgel with enhanced physicochemical stability, topical performance, drug release, skin permeability and antifungal effectiveness. Methods: Drug-excipient compatibility was evaluated by FTIR and DSC and luliconazole was measured by UV spectrophotometry at 296 nm. Solubility screening and necessary hydrophilic-lipophilic balance (RHLB) assessment were carried out to optimize the Tween® 20/Span® 80 emulsifier system. The physicochemical, rheological, mechanical and colloidal characteristics of HPMC and Sepineo™ P600 based emulgels were studied. The in vitro release was evaluated using Strat-M® membrane and the ex vivo penetration with pig ear skin. The antifungal effectiveness against Trichophyton rubrum and Epidermophyton floccosum and preliminary stability of 3 months were investigated. Results: The analytical technique was linear in the range of 2 to 12 µg/mL (R2 = 0.9999). The stable emulgels were obtained using Sepineo™ P600 and S2 (3.5% w/w) was selected as the best formulation. The S2 exhibited pH 5.04, viscosity 3.89 Pa?s, drug content 100.9%, globule size 612±34 nm, PDI 0.318±0.041 and zeta potential ?28.4±2.1 mV. In vitro drug release and ex vivo permeability were found to be 96.19 ± 1.12% and 99.13 ± 0.78% at 8 h, respectively. Inhibition zones were 24.6±1.1 and 22.9±1.3 mm and MIC and MFC values were 0.98 and 1.95 µg/mL. S2 was steady physically for 3 months. Conclusion: The S2 based on Sepineo™ P600 showed good stability, release, penetration, and antifungal performance, enabling its continued development as a luliconazole topical delivery system.

papers.title: Unconventional DNA architecture in a dopamine–bound aptamer complex
papers.abstract: Abstract Aptamers are oligonucleotides that have been selected to bind a particular target. Despite the growing popularity of functional DNA aptamers, there remains limited knowledge of their binding mechanisms, as few have been characterized at the atomic level. Here, we use NMR spectroscopy to obtain structural details of RKEC1, a shortened version of a DNA aptamer previously reported to bind dopamine. We find that RKEC1 forms a compact structure upon ligand binding that lacks any Watson-Crick duplex regions or G-quadruplex core, in stark contrast to nearly all predicted and observed DNA aptamer folds. The atomic details explain dopamine specificity amongst structurally similar compounds, and the determined DNA fold was used to guide biosensor design. The aptamer structure further suggests that DNA folding can access an extensive conformational landscape reminiscent of RNA, thus expanding the diversity traditionally captured by predictive algorithms.

papers.title: Techno-Economic Analysis of Off-Grid Pole-Mounted Photovoltaic Configurations for Accessible and Inaccessible Sites in Arid Climates
papers.abstract: This paper presents an integrated techno-economic synthesis for selecting pole-mounted off-grid photovoltaic configurations, consolidating six experimental and analytical studies into a unified multicriteria decision framework. The analysis is grounded in a one-year high-resolution outdoor experimentation (Aug. 25, 2025 – Aug. 24, 2026) at the QEERI Outdoor Test Facility in Doha, Qatar, complemented by validated analytical models addressing environmental and structural constraints. Five configurations U-IBC 22°, bifacial 22°, U-IBC vertical, bifacial vertical, and an octagonal Vertical Photovoltaic Tube are evaluated for accessible sites with periodic maintenance and inaccessible sites exposed to long-term environmental constraints. A six-criterion composite framework integrates capital efficiency, land-use efficiency, battery storage requirement, soiling and maintenance burden, shading resilience, and structural compactness. Three dimensionless penalty indices for accessibility, shading, and structural impact, along with a compound index, quantify the impacts of real-world constraints. The results reveal a resource–constraint duality: bifacial 22° modules marginally minimize installed capacity under ideal accessible conditions, whereas the Vertical Photovoltaic Tube performs better under constrained scenarios. The accessibility penalty decreases from + 26.90% for tilted configurations to + 1.07% for the Vertical Photovoltaic Tube, representing a 25-fold advantage, while the compound penalty decreases from + 280.7% to + 34.8% under simultaneous zero-access soiling and 50% shading conditions. Above 67% shading, all planar configurations reach complete power-production outage, whereas the Vertical Photovoltaic Tube remains operable. The proposed framework shifts PV system selection from single-metric optimization toward constraint-driven decision-making.

papers.title: IMPACT OF DIGITAL MARKETING ON CONSUMER BEHAVIOUR IN THE TECH AGE: A STUDY WITH SPECIAL REFERENCE TO KANDHAMAL DISTRICT OF ODISHA
papers.abstract: Emerging technologies have made digital marketing the most important form of commercial communication in today’s world. It has changed the ways in which consumers gather information, compare choices, and make purchases. This study focuses on the effects of digital marketing on consumers in the Kandhamal district of Odisha. The district is mainly rural and tribal, and has experienced a recent rise in the availability of the internet. The study employed a descriptive research design, and a structured survey was used to collect primary data from 150 participants. The survey included, among others, social media marketing and online advertising, consumer trust in digital channels, and self-reported behavioral changes. The survey used a 5-point Likert scale. Several statistical analyses were conducted on the data, including, but not limited to, Pearson correlation, multiple regression, and ANOVA. The results of the study demonstrated a high level of awareness of digital marketing and a strong self-reported behavioral impact. From the respondents surveyed, 68.7% claimed that their buying behavior was influenced by digital marketing. Although significant behavioral impacts were reported by female respondents as compared to male respondents (p = .042), and significant effects were found on the Digital Marketing Awareness between rural, semi-urban and urban respondents (p = .041), favorable opinions of digital marketing were not expressed in a measurable way. The study attempts to provide evidence of digital consumer behavior of a region with limited research in the area, and provides marketing, policy, and research recommendations.

papers.title: Machine Learning and Deep Learning for Food Quality Assessment Using Hyperspectral Imaging: Advances, Challenges, and Future Directions
papers.abstract: Abstract Maintaining food quality and safety standards is essential for reducing postharvest losses, sustaining consumer confidence, and meeting international trade requirements. Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) has emerged as a powerful non-destructive technique for assessing both internal and external quality attributes of horticultural products. This review provides a systematic synthesis of recent advances in HSI-based quality assessment of fruits and nuts using machine learning and deep learning approaches. Applications are categorised into defect and non-defect quality attributes, including moisture content, sugar concentration, ripeness, maturity, firmness, nutritional composition, microbial contamination, structural damage, and chemical indicators associated with toxicity and rancidity, such as aflatoxin, free fatty acids (FFAs), and peroxide value (PV). The review critically evaluates spectral preprocessing techniques, modelling approaches, model evaluation criteria, and the influence of sample size and data variability on predictive performance. In addition, commonly reported wavelengths associated with moisture, sugar concentration, firmness, peroxide value, and internal discolouration are systematically compared to identify recurring and overlapping spectral regions across different horticultural products. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first review to demonstrate that multiple quality attributes across fruits and nuts share common important spectral regions, highlighting opportunities for the development of more efficient, transferable, and generalisable HSI models. Finally, key future research directions are identified, including the development of balanced and standardised datasets, transformer-based architectures for improved generalisation, and red-green-blue (RGB) reconstruction of hyperspectral images to enhance interpretability. The advances discussed in this review have strong potential to improve scalability and facilitate wider industrial adoption of HSI technologies for postharvest quality monitoring and food safety assessment.

papers.title: Roadbase performance and modification mechanisms of TBM-excavated gneiss muck utilizing a fiber–geopolymer synergistic stabilization system
papers.abstract: The disposal of TBM muck has become a pressing issue in tunnel construction. This study addresses the utilization of 295,000 m 3 of gneiss muck excavated from the DXL Tunnel in western China by modifying it with low‑calcium fly ash (FA), ground granulated blast‑furnace slag (GGBS), carbide slag (CCS), and basalt fiber (BF) to produce a roadbase material. The optimal mix, designated X‑FGC (FA:GGBS:CCS = 9:4:1 with 0.3% 12‑mm BF), was determined via response surface methodology. Mechanical and durability properties were assessed through unconfined compressive strength (UCS), splitting tensile strength (STS), wet‑dry cycling, and sulfate attack tests; the modification mechanisms were investigated using FTIR, XRD, and SEM. The results show that, after 7 days of curing, the modified muck achieves a UCS of 7.22 MPa and an STS of 0.764 MPa. After 20 wet‑dry cycles and 40 days of sulfate exposure, the UCS loss rates are 11.3% and 4.53%, respectively. Performance enhancement is attributed to the formation of a multi‑gel system (N‑A‑S‑H, C‑A‑S‑H, and C‑S‑H), which cements particles, fills pores, and promotes fiber bridging. However, although increasing the X‑FGC content generates more gels and improves mechanical strength and wet‑dry resistance, it also retards polymerization, reduces the degree of gelation, and impairs sulfate resistance. Overall, X‑FGC exhibits promising mechanical performance and durability as a roadbase material, while incorporating a high proportion of TBM‑excavated gneiss muck (approximately 79% of the total wet‑dry mass in the optimal mixture).

papers.title: Activating Electronic Functionality of Organic Sublattices in Hybrid Perovskites Through Electrostatically Buffered Radical Coupling
papers.abstract: Organic-inorganic hybrid perovskites have emerged as important optoelectronic semiconductors, yet their chemically versatile organic sublattices remain largely electronically inactive. In this study, we introduce electrostatically buffered radical coupling (EBRC) as an alternative electronic-coupling mode for activating organic sublattices. By inserting an electrostatic buffering medium between neighboring organic radicals, EBRC alleviates the intrinsic limitation of direct radical π-stacking, where strong Coulombic repulsion within partially filled radical bands promotes Mott-Hubbard-type localization. Using photochromic viologen-based hybrid perovskites as model systems, we directly compare EBRC with conventional compact radical π-stacking. Counterintuitively, despite the larger intermolecular separation and reduced orbital overlap, the EBRC system exhibits an approximately 100-fold enhancement in conductivity and photocurrent, whereas the compact radical π-stacked counterpart shows only negligible improvement. The EBRC system further increases carrier mobility by approximately 70-fold, facilitates efficient organic-inorganic electron transport, and enables light-induced reversible reconstruction of the band-edge electronic structure. These findings establish electrostatic buffering as a complementary design principle for engineering intermolecular electronic coupling beyond the conventional orbital-overlap paradigm, providing a general framework for activating electronically functional organic sublattices in perovskites and related radical semiconductors.

papers.title: FOXC1–GMDS axis-driven glycolytic reprogramming promotes tumor progression in triple-negative breast cancer
papers.abstract: Abstract Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is a clinically aggressive subtype that is highly reliant on glycolytic metabolism. Despite this well-characterized metabolic feature, the molecular mechanisms governing glycolytic fitness and the therapeutic potential to exploit these metabolic adaptations remain poorly defined. In this study, we pinpoint GDP-mannose 4,6-dehydratase (GMDS) as a transcriptionally regulated metabolic effector that sustains glycolytic fitness and promotes tumorigenesis and progression in TNBC. Multiomic analyses converge to identify GMDS as a pivotal metabolic node in TNBC, while mechanistic investigations demonstrate that the transcription factor FOXC1 drives GMDS expression by directly binding to its promoter region. GMDS induces a glycolytic metabolic state via the cAMP/PKA-CREB-PFKFB2 signaling axis, thereby enhancing the proliferative and metastatic capacities of TNBC cells. Genetic ablation of GMDS impairs glycolytic flux and potently inhibits tumor growth, defining GMDS as a critical metabolic dependency in TNBC. Furthermore, structure-guided screening yields a candidate GMDS inhibitor that recapitulates the phenotypic effects of GMDS depletion and effectively inhibits the progression of TNBC, revealing a pharmacologically actionable metabolic vulnerability. Collectively, our findings establish a FOXC1-GMDS metabolic axis that connects lineage-specific transcriptional control to glycolytic rewiring, and position GMDS as a druggable metabolic effector and precision therapeutic target in TNBC.

papers.title: Therapeutic efficacy and systemic pharmacokinetics of a dual‐drug hydrogel contact lens for sustained glaucoma therapy
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Conventional topical therapy for glaucoma is limited by poor ocular bioavailability, rapid precorneal drug loss, frequent dosing and systemic absorption through the nasolacrimal pathway, which may reduce therapeutic efficacy and increase the risk of adverse effects. Drug-eluting hydrogel contact lenses have emerged as a promising strategy to overcome these limitations by enabling sustained ocular drug delivery. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy, ocular biocompatibility and systemic pharmacokinetic profile of an optimized dual-drug-loaded HEMA-based hydrogel contact lens delivering timolol maleate (TM) and brimonidine tartrate (BT) for sustained glaucoma management. METHODS: Optimized hydrogel contact lenses composed of 2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate (HEMA), N, N-dimethylacrylamide (DMA), N-vinylpyrrolidone (NVP) and ethylene glycol dimethacrylate (EGDMA) were fabricated by UV photopolymerization and loaded with TM and BT (4 mg/mL each). Ocular biocompatibility was assessed using the modified Draize irritation test. Therapeutic efficacy was evaluated in a steroid-induced ocular hypertension New Zealand White rabbit model by monitoring intraocular pressure (IOP) for 24 h. Systemic drug exposure was determined by validated high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) analysis of plasma samples, while ocular safety was further confirmed through histopathological examination. RESULTS: The optimized hydrogel lens exhibited excellent ocular biocompatibility, with a maximum Draize score of 0.33 ± 0.12 that resolved completely within 48 h and no histopathological evidence of ocular tissue damage. In hypertensive rabbits, the dual-drug hydrogel lens maintained normotensive IOP (16.1 ± 0.8 mmHg) for 24 h, representing a 43.5% reduction from baseline and significantly outperforming conventional eye drops beyond 4 h (p < 0.01). Plasma concentrations of both TM and BT remained below the limit of quantification (<2.0 ng/mL) throughout the study, whereas conventional eye drops produced measurable systemic exposure (TM: 18.4 ± 2.1 ng/mL; BT: 8.2 ± 1.2 ng/mL), demonstrating effective minimization of systemic drug absorption. CONCLUSION: The optimized dual-drug-loaded hydrogel contact lens provided sustained intraocular pressure reduction, excellent ocular biocompatibility and negligible systemic drug exposure compared with conventional topical therapy. These findings highlight its potential as a sustained ocular drug-delivery platform capable of improving therapeutic efficacy, reducing systemic adverse effects and enhancing long-term treatment adherence in glaucoma management. Further long-term preclinical investigations and clinical studies are warranted to support clinical translation.

papers.title: Functional characterization and industrial suitability assessment of protein isolates from Moroccan faba bean varieties
papers.abstract: Plant-based proteins have gained increasing attention as nutritious and sustainable alternatives to animal-derived ingredients. In the current study, the thermal and techno-functional properties of protein isolates from eight Moroccan faba bean varieties (Aguadulce, Defes, Hiba, Lobab, Alfia5, Alfia17, Alfia21, and Zina) were compared to evaluate their potential application in the food industry. Following protein extraction and characterization using Kjeldahl, FT-IR, and SDS-PAGE, the water retention capacity (WRC), oil holding capacity (OHC), emulsifying properties, foaming properties, gelation properties, and colour parameters of flours and protein isolates were measured. Thermal analysis of the protein isolates revealed two distinct endothermic peaks, attributed to protein denaturation (Tm, 120.2–130.8 °C) and to thermal degradation (Td, 223.8–230.2 °C). Compared with their flours, the protein isolates showed lower whiteness and flour colour index and higher yellowness and browning indices, most markedly in Alfia5 and least in Aguadulce. Both the fraction (flour, protein isolate) and variety had a significant effect on the functional properties ( p < 0.05). Moreover, Alfia21 was found to exhibit the highest WRC (193%), foaming capacity (FC) (89.37%), and emulsion activity index (EAI) (83.4 m 2 /g). On the other hand, Lobab showed the best OHC (124.70%) and emulsion stability index (ESI) (85.89 min). Based on its functional profile, Alfia21 emerged as the most promising candidate for bakery products, meat analogues and beverages, these applications being predicted from the measured functional properties rather than validated in food formulations. These results provide a basis for the valorization of locally adapted faba bean varieties as affordable plant-based protein ingredients, in a context where the diversification of protein sources is of growing relevance for food security and sustainable consumption.

papers.title: Failure Analysis of Steel Wire‐Reinforced Composite Pipes for Gas Field Flowback Fluid
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT To clarify the failure mechanism of steel wire‐reinforced thermoplastic (SWRTP) pipes in flowback fluid pipelines, failed and intact samples were systematically investigated. Compression cracking and hydraulic burst tests confirmed the original intact pipe met standard requirements. The failed pipe exhibited circumferential cracking near the metal joint, displaying environmental stress cracking (ESC) characteristics. Morphological and spectroscopic analyses revealed complex electrochemical corrosion of the steel wires driven by CO 2 , HCO 3 − , and SO 4 2− species from the penetrating fluid. Furthermore, thermal analysis showed a localized oxidation induction temperature (OIT) decrease at the fracture surface (209.84°C), suggesting but not definitively proving service‐induced antioxidant depletion. The failure is proposed to be ESC, possibly attributed to metal‐joint crimping stress and the flowback chemical environment synergistically degrading the resin matrix. Crucially, it is hypothesized that antioxidant depletion and crack propagation mutually accelerated localized polymer embrittlement. Subsequent fluid ingress caused severe electrochemical corrosion of the steel wires, drastically reducing the pipe's pressure‐bearing capacity and ultimately leading to inside‐out penetrating cracks.

papers.title: Suppressing Irreversible Interfacial Spatial Electron Transfer for High‐Temperature 4.6 V LiCoO 2
papers.abstract: (LCO) cathodes under elevated temperatures is essential for meeting the growing energy-storage demands across diverse applications. However, it is severely hindered by interfacial parasitic reactions arising from irreversible electron transfer between electrolyte solvents and the cathode. Herein, we demonstrate the regulation of the spatial distance and orientation of phosphate solvent molecules within the electric double layer at the LCO interface, thereby fundamentally suppressing irreversible interfacial spatial electron transfer (ISET) under combined high-voltage and high-temperature conditions. The fluorinated bidentate phosphate ester (TEFP) creates a compact solvation sheath that counteracts the interfacial-electric-field-driven enrichment of phosphate solvents, increases the solvent-cathode distance, and maintains a P═O orientation away from the cathode, thereby suppressing ISET from the P═O bond to the delithiated LCO. This simultaneously promotes the formation of a well-controlled, uniform, and stable cathode-electrolyte interphase. Consequently, Li||LCO cells with TEFP electrolyte deliver superior cycling stability at 4.6 V and elevated temperatures, with 80% capacity retention after 760 cycles at 60°C and 75.5% after 300 cycles at 80°C, while Ah-level pouch cells further validate the practical viability of the electrolyte. This work provides guidance for the design of cathode interfaces under high-voltage and high-temperature conditions.

papers.title: An integrated cathode-electrolyte architecture with Cu dual active-sites for all-solid-state Li–CO2 batteries
papers.abstract: All-solid-state Li–CO2 batteries are limited by sluggish interfacial CO2 redox kinetics and the incomplete decomposition of insulating Li2CO3 at rigid solid-solid-gas interfaces. Here, we report an integrated cathode-electrolyte architecture in which copper atomic clusters and single atoms are co-anchored on freestanding N-doped carbon nanotubes and coupled with a succinonitrile/Li1+xAlyGe2-y(PO4)3-based solid-state electrolyte. The conformal ion-conducting phase and conductive nanotube scaffold provide coupled pathways for Li+, electrons and CO2 at the cathode interface. Electronic coupling between the copper atomic clusters and single atoms induces charge transfer from the former to the latter (~0.457 e−), rendering the Cu cluster sites partially cationic and facilitating the activation of carbonate intermediates. This dual-site configuration changes the discharge pathway and lowers the reaction energy of the rate-determining step to 2.412 eV. The assembled battery delivers a discharge capacity of 21356 mAh g−1 at 200 mA g−1 and operates for 260 cycles (>1000 h) at 500 mA g−1 with an energy efficiency of 78%. This work provides an interfacial design strategy for solid-state Li–CO2 batteries by coupling continuous transport pathways with electronically regulated dual Cu active sites. Stimuli responsive assemblies can offer precise control over behaviour, but use of gases for this control is rare. Here, the authors report the use of carbon dioxide for tuneable nanoparticle response, directed by changes in peptide structure.

papers.title: Toward net-zero building: an optimisation methodology for passive and active retrofits with renewable integration – a UK office building case study
papers.abstract: Existing commercial buildings account for a large share of energy use and carbon emissions, highlighting the need for net-zero retrofit strategies. This study develops an integrated framework for building retrofits, combining calibrated building energy simulation with multi-source renewable energy system design and optimisation to reduce energy demand, maximise on-site renewable generation, and enable cost-effective decarbonisation. A calibrated energy model was created in DesignBuilder to evaluate retrofit measures, while renewable energy systems and storage were optimised for maximum renewable fractions using HOMER Pro. A two-stage MATLAB-based Pareto front and TOPSIS multi-criteria optimisation evaluated and ranked retrofit configurations. The framework was applied to a UK office building case study (hot-summer, cold-winter climate), identifying the optimal configuration, which combines lighting upgrades, office equipment improvements, a water-to-water ground-source heat pump, carport-mounted solar PV, and rooftop horizontal-axis wind turbines. The retrofit reduces annual energy demand by 38.4% and achieves an average renewable fraction of 66.3%, reducing net grid energy import by 91.53%, with on-site generation exceeding demand during peak summer months. Annual CO 2 emissions decrease by 39.0% after retrofitting and by 86.1% after the integration of renewables compared to the baseline model of the case-study building. Economic analysis shows strong financial viability, with a levelized cost of £0.172/kWh and a payback period of 6.48 years. Sensitivity analyses confirm the solution remains optimal under varying energy prices and stakeholder priorities, demonstrating robustness for commercial deployment. The results highlight the framework's ability to guide transferable, multi-criteria retrofit planning and support deep operational decarbonisation across diverse building types.

papers.title: Surface Ion-imprinted Magnetic Halloysite Nano Clay Composite with Double Specific Binding Sites for Selective Extraction and Preconcentration of Cadmium and Lead in Water
papers.abstract: Abstract A dual-template magnetic ion-imprinted polymer based on halloysite (Fe₃O₄@HNT-DIIP) was synthesised via surface imprinting and co-precipitation. This material was utilised in magnetic solid-phase extraction (MSPE) to selectively and simultaneously concentrate cadmium (Cd 2+ ) and lead (Pb 2+ ) from both aqueous samples and environmental water sources. The morphological structure, crystallinity, and surface characteristics were analysed using Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and a zetasizer. The maximum adsorption capacities of Fe 3 O 4 @HNT-DIIP for Cd 2+ and Pb 2+ ions were 44.4 and 58.5 mg/g. The adsorption kinetics exhibited a strong correlation with the pseudo-second-order model, and the Langmuir isotherm suggested that the Fe 3 O 4 @HNT-DIIP adsorbent facilitates monolayer sorption on uniform sites. The Fe 3 O 4 @HNT-DIIP adsorbent proved selective towards Cd 2+ and Pb 2+ ions in the presence of Co 2+ and Zn 2+ . Under optimum conditions, the Fe 3 O 4 @HNT-DIIP-MSPE coupled with inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) exhibited wide linear ranges (0.712-100), acceptable limits of quantification (LOQs = 0.712–1.45 µg/L) and limit of detection (LODs = 0.214–0.440 µg/L) for Cd 2+ and Pb 2+ ions. The proposed method demonstrated excellent performance in preconcentrating and detecting trace metals in surface and groundwater samples, yielding recoveries of 95.5–102%.

papers.title: Time‐Resolved Multidimensional NMR Spectroscopy Reveals the Bifurcated Folding Pathway of a Thrombin‐Binding DNA G4–Azobenzene Derivative Complex
papers.abstract: Resolving the complex folding landscape of biomolecules contributes greatly to understanding cellular function, since cellular regulation and signal transduction are often linked to their conformational dynamics. We here investigate conformational transitions of a DNA deoxyguanosine G-quadruplex (G4) induced by binding of a low molecular weight azobenzene derivative. This ligand acts as a photoswitch that triggers conformational rearrangements of the thrombin binding aptamer (TBA) G4 in a reversible manner pending on the photoisomeric state of the ligand (E- or Z-configuration). We exploit the reversible association-dissociation of the photoactive ligand to extend current real-time NMR experiments, allowing the in-depth characterization of the folding pathways for the ligand association and dissociation processes and induction of G4 refolding. The folding pathway features kinetic partitioning and significant population of G4 folding intermediates.

papers.title: Green-synthesised silver nanoparticle-loaded alginate/gelatin/aloe vera nanocomposite hydrogel films as wound dressings
papers.journal: Frontiers in Life Sciences and Related Technologies
papers.abstract: Open wounds resulting from trauma, burns or complications of diabetes require dressings that keep the wound bed moist, limit infection and remain compatible with host tissue. Many reported hydrogel dressings satisfy some of these requirements but are limited by high cost, complex synthesis, weak mechanical behaviour or poor cytocompatibility. Although alginate, gelatin, Aloe vera and silver nanoparticles have each been used individually in dressing materials, their combination into a single, low-cost film, and the systematic study of how the alginate-to-gelatin ratio governs its properties with green-synthesised AgNPs, has not previously been reported. In this study, three nanocomposite hydrogel films based on alginate, gelatin and Aloe vera were prepared at ALG/GEL/AV mass ratios of 1/3/20, 2/2/20 and 3/1/20 (coded AGA13, AGA22 and AGA31, respectively), crosslinked with Ca²⁺ and loaded with 1% (w/w) silver nanoparticles. The AgNPs were green synthesised by reducing AgNO₃ with pomegranate (Punica granatum) extract; they were spherical, approximately 50-150 nm in size, with a mean hydrodynamic radius of 162.76 nm and a zeta potential of -41.83 mV, indicating a stable, weakly aggregating dispersion. Film behaviour was largely governed by the alginate content. As the alginate fraction increased, the films became denser and swelled less, so that equilibrium swelling and water retention both decreased in the order AGA13>AGA22>AGA31, with AGA13 reaching approximately 150% swelling and 65% water retention. Ethanol displacement indicated negligible open porosity for all films, in line with SEM. Over four weeks the films lost mass from about 78% (AGA13) to below 40% (AGA31), a range wide enough to match dressing lifetime to the intended application. None of the formulations was cytotoxic to L-929 fibroblasts in the indirect MTT assay, with viabilities of 115%, 110% and above 130% for AGA13, AGA22 and AGA31 relative to the control. Overall, AGA31 combined the slowest mass loss with the strongest fibroblast response, identifying it as the most suitable candidate for longer-term wound management.

papers.title: Synergistic Interaction Engineering Enables Homogeneous Mixed‐Cation Perovskite Single Crystals for High‐Performance X‐Ray Detection
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Mixed A‐site compositions are an effective route to boost the x‐ray detection performance of perovskite single crystals, yet their growth is often accompanied by pronounced spatial compositional inhomogeneity. This macroscopic phase segregation originates from mismatched formation energies and crystallization kinetics among the different cation components, leading to internal composition gradients that hinder carrier transport but are rarely addressed in perovskite single‐crystal research. Here, we report an acetic acid‐enabled synergistic interaction‐engineering strategy for growing phase‐homogeneous mixed‐cation perovskite single crystals. Acetic acid simultaneously lowers the formation barrier of the formamidinium‐rich phase and suppresses the rapid assembly of the methylammonium‐rich phase, thereby balancing their crystallization rates and eliminating compositional gradients across the crystal. Owing to the improved uniformity and crystal quality, x‐ray detectors based on these single crystals deliver a sensitivity of 3.54 × 10 6 µC Gy −1 cm −2 , a low detection limit of 2.65 nGy s −1 , and excellent operational stability. This kinetic‐regulation concept offers a practical pathway to homogeneous mixed‐cation perovskite single crystals and supports their use in low‐dose, high‐performance optoelectronic devices.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal patterns and nonlinear correlates of coordination between the digital economy and tourism ecological security in Chinese cities
papers.abstract: Tourism ecological security (TES) is essential for sustaining destination resilience, ecological quality, and long-term tourism development. The digital economy (DE) plays a crucial role in improving TES by enabling smart monitoring, efficient resource allocation, and precision governance. Conversely, enhanced TES creates green demand and application scenarios for digital technologies, thereby facilitating DE upgrading. However, existing studies have mainly examined the one-way effects of DE on tourism or ecological performance, with limited attention to the bidirectional coupling coordination between DE and TES and its nonlinear correlates. Using panel data for 206 Chinese cities from 2006 to 2023, this study measures DE and TES using CRITIC and entropy-weighted TOPSIS, respectively; calculates the DE–TES coupling coordination degree (CCD); and combines kernel density estimation, Jenks natural breaks, and XGBoost–SHAP to examine its spatiotemporal evolution and associations with influencing factors. The results show that DE–TES CCD increased continuously, shifting from incoordination toward coordination, while displaying high values in eastern coastal urban agglomerations and lower values in central and western regions. Its influencing factors exhibit nonlinear associations, threshold patterns, and interactions in the model. Residents' educational attainment, tourism resource attractiveness, industrial structure upgrading, and population density are the key influencing factors, with educational attainment showing the strongest explanatory power. The interaction between tourism resource attractiveness and industrial structure upgrading is particularly prominent, indicating that higher tourism resource attractiveness is more positively associated with DE–TES CCD at higher levels of industrial structure upgrading. This study advances the theoretical understanding of DE–TES synergistic evolution and provides evidence for differentiated digital transformation and TES governance in tourism destinations.

papers.title: Thermoluminescence and Kinetic Parameters of a Synthesized Copper-doped LTB Phosphor using High Temperature Solid State Technique
papers.journal: IPS Journal of Engineering and Technology
papers.abstract: Lithium tetraborate is a known thermoluminescent materials with tissue equivalent properties and a promising potential of being used in radiation dosimetry. But, the intensity of the signal in most cases is not suitable for practical purposes. Hence, by way of optimization, this present study prepared lithium tetraborate phosphor and doped with various concentrations of copper dopant (0 – 0.5) % using the high temperature solid state technique and sintering in a programmable Muffle Furnace. The samples were characterized using XRD, FTIR, DTA and SEM/EDX. The SEM, XRD and FTIR confirmed the morphological and structural composition of the phosphors. The EDX confirmed the elemental composition of the samples and DTA established the thermal stability of the crystals. The samples were irradiated with 137Cs at a dose of 7 mGy/h and read in a TLD reader at a constant heating rate of 5 K/s to determine its thermoluminescence and kinetic parameters. The results showed a single broad peak at a temperature of about 855 K and 858 K with no fading peaks. First-order kinetics was obtained for 0.1 % LTB:Cu and 0.5 % LTB:Cu, with the trap depth of 4.4 eV and 2.8 eV, respectively. A symmetry factor of 0.29 and 0.24 was obtained, respectively for 0.1 % copper doped phosphors and 0.5 % copper doped phosphor.

papers.title: Mechanochemically immobilized supported ionic liquid catalysts enable atmospheric-pressure cycloaddition of CO₂ with epoxides
papers.abstract: The conversion of carbon dioxide into value added chemicals is a promising strategy for advancing carbon circularity, yet the development of recyclable catalysts that remain highly active under atmospheric CO 2 pressure without solvents or co-catalysts remains a significant challenge. Herein, we report a mechanochemically synthesized supported ionic liquid catalyst, N(CH 3 ) 2 -[Im][Br]@SiO 2 , that combines the catalytic efficiency of imidazolium ionic liquids with the practical advantages of heterogeneous catalysis. Solid-state 29 Si CP-MAS NMR spectroscopy, supported by Gaussian peak deconvolution and quantitative integration analysis of the T- and Q-type silicon species, confirmed the successful covalent immobilization of the ionic liquid on the silica surface via formation of Si-O-Si(C) linkages, producing an efficient catalyst for the solvent free cycloaddition of CO 2 with epoxides. Under atmospheric CO 2 pressure, the catalyst achieves 99% conversion of epichlorohydrin with 99% yield of chloromethyl ethylene carbonate at 120 °C after 12 h without the need for additional co-catalysts. The high activity originates from cooperative activation of the epoxide through hydrogen bonding by the acidic C2-H proton of the imidazolium cation together with nucleophilic ring opening by the bromide anion. The catalyst retains high activity over five consecutive reaction cycles and exhibits broad substrate scope, delivering consistently high conversions and cyclic carbonate yields (>95%) for structurally diverse epoxides. This work demonstrates that mechanochemical immobilization provides an effective platform for designing recoverable supported ionic liquid catalysts that overcome the traditional trade-off between catalytic performance and recyclability, offering a practical route towards low pressure CO 2 utilization and sustainable cyclic carbonate synthesis.

papers.title: Effective Porosity and Pore–Ligament Architecture in Mg‐Based Solid‐State Hydrogen Storage
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Magnesium (Mg)‐based hydrides offer high gravimetric capacity, high volumetric hydrogen density, elemental abundance, and low material cost, but their practical performance is constrained by coupled hydrogen transport, interfacial reaction, heat transfer, and structural evolution during repeated magnesium/magnesium hydride conversion. This mini‐review reframes porosity as a functional rather than purely morphological attribute. We critically synthesize representative precursor‐derived, scaffold‐free, and layered porous Mg architectures, and organize the available structural, transport, conversion, thermal, and cycling evidence around an operational definition of effective porosity: the gas‐accessible pore fraction that, at a specified structural and reaction state, satisfies a stated molecular‐hydrogen transport criterion within a specified timescale and is spatially coupled to internally converting regions of a percolating Mg‐rich solid domain. Strict three‐dimensional determination is distinguished from intermediate spatial validation and routine laboratory proxies to clarify what can and cannot be inferred experimentally. The analysis shows that high initial porosity, high surface area, or rapid powder kinetics alone do not establish storage‐relevant functionality. Secondary phases must be assigned process‐specific roles rather than inferred from coexistence, and apparent activation energies in shaped media may reflect coupled reaction, transport, and thermal effects. The resulting design principle is to preserve gas access, Mg‐rich continuity, internal conversion, thermal contact, and structural integrity simultaneously through shaping and cycling.

papers.title: Predicting fish spoilage through adsorption and detection of volatile sulfur compounds on B2N monolayers: a computational study
papers.abstract: In the present work, a comprehensive density functional theory (DFT) investigation was conducted to elucidate the adsorption behavior of two key sulfur-containing volatile compounds generated during fish deterioration, namely dimethyl sulfide (DMS, CH₃–S–CH₃) and dimethyl disulfide (DMDS, CH₃–S–S–CH₃). The calculated adsorption energies are significantly negative, revealing strong yet reversible adsorption characteristics suitable for both sensing and capture applications. The obtained E ads (%ΔE g ) values for DMS/B₂N and DMDS/B₂N are − 0.47 eV (40%) and − 0.45 eV (39%), respectively. Adsorption induces substantial modulation of the B₂N electronic band gap, generating distinct electronic responses for each analyte. As a result, the monolayer exhibits distinct electronic and φ-type sensing responses, arising from substantial band-gap modulation and charge transfer between the adsorbed species and the B₂N substrate, thereby providing a pronounced and readily detectable electrical response. The pristine B₂N surface exhibits high sensitivity toward both DMS and DMDS, while the short recovery times and ultrafast desorption confirm excellent reversibility. Therefore, the B₂N monolayer serves as a multifunctional nanomaterial, acting as both a high-performance sensor and an efficient adsorbent for sulfur-based spoilage compounds, and presents a promising strategy for real-time seafood freshness monitoring.

papers.title: Antifibrinolytic Agent: Synthesis and Characterization of Cocrystal and Salts of Tranexamic Acid
papers.abstract: Abstract Tranexamic acid (TXA) is a potent antifibrinolytic agent with poor oral bioavailability (∼35–40%) due to its high polarity and zwitterionic nature, while physicochemical factors, including its structural instability, further hinder its absorption. In this study, the crystal engineering concept is applied to enhance the physicochemical properties of TXA through targeted structural modifications, resulting in the synthesis of pharmaceutically stable cocrystal and salt forms. The application of supramolecular synthon design, pKa rule, and structural geometry (molecular mimicry), resulted in the rational design, synthesis, and structural characterization of eight binary multicomponent forms of TXA: a TXA-adipate salt, monoclinic space group P21/n; a TXA-salicylate salt, monoclinic space group P21/n; a TXA-picolinate salt, monoclinic space group P21/c; a TXA-acetaminophen cocrystal hydrate, monoclinic space group P21; a TXA-malonate salt, orthorhombic space group Pbca; a TXA-maleate salt hydrate, monoclinic space group P21/c; a TXA-malate salt, monoclinic space group P21/c; and a TXA-citrate salt, triclinic space group P1̅ These multicomponent forms were obtained via different hydrogen bonding interactions, some of them charge-assisted (N–H···O, N+–H···O–, O–H···O, and O–H···O–) between NH2 and/or −OH groups of TXA and the carboxyl (−C(O−)═O) functional groups of the coformers. In the cocrystals, TXA exists as zwitterions (zero charge), whereas in the salts, it carries a positive charge due to the protonation of its carboxylic (−COOH) and ammonium (−NH3+) groups. The NH3+ to COO– charge-assisted H-bond provides stabilization to both the coformer COO– as well as the TXA’s NH3+. Solid-state characterization using Raman and FT-Raman spectroscopy, thermal techniques (DSC), and X-ray diffraction analysis (powder and single-crystal XRD) supports and confirms the structural novelty. The superior stability profiles of the new TXA cocrystal and salts under standard conditions (40 °C ± 2 °C, 75% ± 5% RH) establish an improved structure–property profile compared to pure TXA.

papers.title: Polyurethane Recycling Using Catalytic Pyrolysis: Insights into Catalyst Stability
papers.abstract: Abstract Polyurethanes are widely used in many applications because of their versatility. However, efficient recycling remains challenging. Recent findings indicate that aniline recovery from rigid polyurethane foams via catalytic pyrolysis with an alumina-based catalyst is an attractive option. Techno-economic analyses showed that catalyst costs are a major factor and that catalyst recycling is essential. Here, we report an extensive study on the recyclability of a selected alumina-based catalyst (Puralox 5/200) for the catalytic pyrolysis of PUR. Experiments with fresh and spent catalysts in a batch-operated staged free-fall reactor at gram scale (3.0 g nPUR, catalyst-to-feed ratio: 1 to 1, 550 °C) using virgin PUR showed differences in activity and chemoselectivity for aniline, indicative of catalyst deactivation. Spent catalyst characterization (TGA–MS, TEM–EDX, N2 physisorption, TPD, and XRD) showed hard coke (14.4 wt %) on the catalyst. Catalyst regeneration was successfully demonstrated using an oxidative treatment at 550 °C, though some irreversible deactivation, including loss in acidity and Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface area, as well as inorganic accumulation, was observed after five regeneration/recycles. Additional experiments to assess catalyst performance after multiple regeneration-recycles were carried out on a milligram scale in a tandem microreactor coupled to GC–MS/FID (catalyst-to-feed ratio of 5:1 at 550 °C), using rigid polyurethane (nPUR) and a contaminated end-of-life (EOL) feed. With nPUR, catalyst performance for aniline and toluidine formation declined in the first 4 cycles, then stabilized at half the original activity for 28 cycles, and finally dropped to very low levels. For EOL PUR, catalyst performance over multiple runs was significantly worse, and the catalyst was inactive after 18 cycles. We characterized the spent catalysts from both PUR feeds (a.o TEM–EDX), which showed that inorganic impurity accumulation contributes to catalyst deactivation.

papers.title: Ion and particle size distribution measurements in the Indo-Gangetic Plain: seasonal insights and challenges in new particle formation event characterization
papers.abstract: Abstract. New particle formation (NPF) is a major source of atmospheric aerosols and cloud condensation nuclei, influencing climate and air quality. In highly polluted regions such as the Indo-Gangetic Plain (IGP), where precursor concentrations and condensation sinks are among the highest globally, NPF remains poorly constrained due to limited observations of particles and ions in sub–10 nm size range. Here, we investigated the occurrence and microphysical evolution of NPF at a suburban IGP site (CAS-AO, Sonipat, Haryana), during May – December 2023 using ion and particle measurements together with meteorological data. NPF events are frequent during summer and less common in winter. The weak seasonal variability of ion concentrations relative to nucleation-mode particles suggests that neutral pathways dominate NPF in this high-sink environment. The median condensation sinks on event-days (0.024 s⁻¹) are approximately half those on non-event days (0.046 s⁻¹). Particle growth rates (maximum concentration method) increase with size, from 14.7 nm h⁻¹ (3–7 nm) to 19.0 nm h⁻¹ (7–20 nm), indicating size-dependent condensational growth. In this high-background setting, pollution plumes, and meteorological variability intermittently mask or distort NPF signals, limiting the direct applicability of both visual and automated classification methods and growth rate estimation methods. Our observations highlight that careful application and improvement of data analysis methods, along with precursor gas measurements, are required to better constrain nucleation processes by avoiding methodological sensitivity due to the complexity of aerosol dynamic processes in multi-source, high-condensation-sink environments, such as IGP.

papers.title: CO2-induced formation of polymeric ionic liquids from structurally related hydroxyl-functional amidines
papers.abstract: Hydroxyl-functional amidines provide a single-component platform in which CO 2 fixation generates ionic functionality and promotes intermolecular organization. Here, structurally related amidines derived from serinol and isoserinol were compared as precursors of CO 2 -responsive polymeric ionic liquids (PILs). Direct treatment of the neat amidines with CO 2 resulted in the formation of CO 2 -derived ionic structures consistent with amidinium–alkyl carbonate units and their subsequent intermolecular association. Time-resolved 1 H NMR and FTIR spectroscopy showed progressive development of the CO 2 -derived ionic state, while 13 C NMR supported the presence of alkyl carbonate and protonated amidinium carbon environments. The two systems exhibited distinct transformation profiles. Isoserinol-derived PIL-2 showed a faster initial spectroscopic response, a more rapid change in the local microenvironment detected by pyrene fluorescence, and earlier stabilization of relative viscosity. GPC indicated a greater contribution of higher apparent molecular-size species in PIL-2, consistent with more pronounced intermolecular association. After 60 min, Amidine-2 captured 2.43 mmol g −1 CO 2 , compared with 1.63 mmol g −1 for Amidine-1. Principal component analysis further distinguished the systems based on their spectroscopic and physicochemical responses. DFT calculations showed that Amidine-2 has a higher molecular dipole moment and a shorter OH···N separation involving the secondary hydroxyl group, providing a molecular basis for its stronger response to CO 2 . These results indicate that the relative arrangement of hydroxyl and amidine functionalities influences both CO 2 fixation and the association of the resulting CO 2 -derived ionic units into extended structures.

papers.title: A Phenomenological Inquiry into Post-Traumatic Growth Among Nurses Who Worked on the Frontline of COVID-19
papers.journal: Journal of Modern Nursing Practice and Research
papers.abstract: Objective: Research has demonstrated significant adverse psychological outcomes among nurses working on the frontline during the COVID-19 pandemic. However, some nurses also experienced post-traumatic growth (PTG) while navigating these experiences. This study aimed to identify the key elements that facilitated PTG among nurses who worked on the frontline in the UK during the pandemic and to explore what nurses believed policymakers and practitioners could do to support growth in others negatively affected by frontline work. Methods: A qualitative design was used to explore participants’ subjective lived experiences. Twelve nurses who had worked closely with COVID-19 patients in UK hospitals were recruited through professional organisations, nursing support groups, professional and personal networks, participant snowballing, and NHS Staff Wellbeing Hubs. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analysed using Template Analysis, guided initially by an a priori coding template derived from existing PTG literature while allowing themes to emerge inductively from participants’ accounts. Results: Four top-level themes were identified: individual characteristics, coping strategies, organisational and environmental considerations, and interpersonal factors. Participants described reflective and self-aware qualities, compassion, advocacy, previous experiences of difficulty, and work-related characteristics as relevant to their experiences of growth. Coping mechanisms included boundary setting, mindfulness, avoidance, emotional numbness, and consideration of mortality. Organisational and environmental factors included camaraderie, moments of joy, opportunities for learning and development, good leadership, and access to psychological support. Interpersonal factors included professional and personal relationships, community acts of kindness, and appropriate psychological support. Participants also identified the importance of long-term support, improved access to psychological services, and changes to aspects of NHS culture. Conclusion: PTG among frontline nurses appears to involve an interaction between individual characteristics, coping strategies, relationships, and the organisational and environmental context. The findings suggest that support should be responsive to individual needs and should provide opportunities for nurses to process and make meaning of distressing experiences. Trauma-informed leadership, appropriate psychological support, and opportunities for reflection and debriefing may help support nurses following experiences of frontline work.
papers.summary: Objective: Research has demonstrated significant adverse psychological outcomes among nurses working on the frontline during the COVID-19 pandemic. Organisational and environmental factors included camaraderie, moments of joy, opportunities for learning and development, good leadership, and access to psychological support. The findings suggest that support should be responsive to individual needs and should provide opportunities for nurses to process and make meaning of distressing experiences.

papers.title: Photodynamic inactivation and photodynamic therapy for viral pathogens: a systematic review of antiviral efficacy, mechanisms, and translational boundaries
papers.abstract: Background and Aim Viral infections pose a persistent global threat, driven by emerging pathogens and rising antiviral resistance. Photodynamic inactivation (PDI) and photodynamic therapy (PDT) generate reactive oxygen species via a photosensitizer (PS) and light, offering broad-spectrum antiviral potential. However, evidence on efficacy remains fragmented and spans mechanistically distinct applications ranging from ex vivo pathogen reduction to localized clinical treatment. This systematic review synthesizes available data on photosensitizer-mediated antiviral effects, therapeutic applications, and limitations, explicitly distinguishing PDI (ex vivo/environmental inactivation) from PDT (in vivo treatment). Methods This systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines. A comprehensive literature search was performed in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase for studies published between January 1990 and April 2026. Peer-reviewed original articles evaluating the antiviral effects of photosensitizer-mediated PDI or PDT in vitro, in vivo, or in clinical settings were included. Studies employing direct UV irradiation without a photosensitizer or light-independent antiviral mechanisms were excluded from the primary evidence synthesis. Two reviewers independently screened studies, assessed eligibility, and extracted data. Due to substantial heterogeneity in viral targets, photosensitizers (PSs), light parameters, and outcome measures, findings were synthesized narratively. Risk of bias was assessed using design-appropriate tools. Results Of 242 records, 30 studies (22 in vitro/ex vivo, 4 animal, and 4 clinical) were included. PDI achieved multi-log reductions against enveloped viruses, while non-enveloped viruses required higher PS concentrations and light doses. Common PSs included methylene blue, porphyrins, phthalocyanines, and Rose Bengal, riboflavin, and ruthenium complexes. Based on the limited and heterogeneous clinical data available, the safety profile of PDI in transfusion-related applications and PDT in mucocutaneous applications appears promising but remains to be conclusively established. Conclusion Photosensitizer-mediated PDI exhibits potent in vitro antiviral activity, particularly against enveloped viruses, through oxidative damage to viral components. However, the evidence is almost entirely preclinical, and current evidence does not support conventional PDT as a clinically feasible treatment for systemic viremia; its most realistic antiviral applications remain localized accessible infections and ex vivo pathogen reduction. Future extracorporeal or targeted light-delivery strategies may eventually expand these boundaries, but no such approach has yet been clinically validated. Further clinical studies are warranted for specific indications, particularly ex vivo blood product decontamination and localized mucocutaneous infections.

However, the evidence is almost entirely preclinical, and current evidence does not support conventional PDT as a clinically feasible treatment for systemic viremia; its most realistic antiviral applications remain localized accessible infections and ex vivo pathogen reduction.

papers.title: Performance enhancement of concentric annular heat exchangers by adopting constructal T-Y-fins: Numerical studies via composite-function, ANN and NSGA-Ⅱ
papers.abstract: Small concentric annular heat exchangers are widely used in compact thermal systems, but their performance is limited by weak convective mixing in the annulus. Constructal T-Y-fins have improved heat removal in flat and single-side geometries; however, their behavior in a conjugate annular configuration, together with the thermal-hydraulic trade-off, remains unclear. This study introduces constructal T-Y-fins into a small concentric annular heat exchanger and evaluates their thermal-hydraulic performance under parallel- and counter-flow conditions. With fixed total volume and fin material, two-degree-of-freedom constructal design is performed, and multi-objective optimization is carried out using an artificial neural network, the NSGA-II algorithm and three decision-making approaches. Under parallel-flow, the optimal composite function value is 0.941, which is 5.9% lower than the reference and 25.2% lower than the model without fins. Under counter-flow, the corresponding value is 0.920 (8% lower than the reference and 27.1% lower than the model without fins), indicating superior performance. The Shannon Entropy DMA yields the smallest deviation indices (0.3816 for parallel-flow, 0.3920 for counter-flow). The maximum thermal driving force concentrates at the branched-fin tips, where the temperature gradient increases by order of magnitude, indicating that flow-field redirection and boundary-layer thinning, rather than surface extension alone, dominate the enhancement.

Under counter-flow, the corresponding value is 0.920 (8% lower than the reference and 27.1% lower than the model without fins), indicating superior performance.

papers.title: DELAYED CATARACT SURGERY IN RURAL AND UNDERSERVED POPULATIONS: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF BARRIERS, CLINICAL CONSEQUENCES, AND STRATEGIES TO IMPROVE SURGICAL UPTAKE
papers.journal: The International Journal of Medical Science and Health Research
papers.abstract: Background: Delayed cataract surgery remains an important barrier to reducing avoidable visual impairment in rural and underserved populations. Delay may occur through delayed presentation, delayed acceptance, or prolonged non-utilization. Objective: To systematically review barriers, clinical consequences, and strategies associated with delayed cataract surgery in rural and underserved populations. Methods: A systematic review was conducted of studies evaluating delayed presentation, delayed uptake, or non-utilization of cataract surgery or related services. Data were extracted on barriers, clinical consequences, and strategies to improve surgical uptake. Findings were synthesized descriptively. Results: Twenty-six studies published from 1991 to 2024 were included. The most frequently reported barriers were financial constraints, geographic and transportation difficulties, lack of perceived need, inadequate knowledge, fear of surgery, and limited family or social support. Delayed or untreated cataract was frequently associated with substantial visual impairment and blindness, with advanced cataract and lens-related complications reported in some settings. Strategies included financial assistance, transportation support, counselling, community education, outreach, and decentralized services. Regular same-location outreach was associated with higher surgical acceptance in one South Indian study. Conclusions: Delayed cataract surgery is multifactorial, involving financial and geographic barriers, perceived need, knowledge, fear, and social support. Multicomponent strategies addressing affordability, accessibility, and counselling may improve surgical uptake.
papers.summary: Background: Delayed cataract surgery remains an important barrier to reducing avoidable visual impairment in rural and underserved populations. Methods: A systematic review was conducted of studies evaluating delayed presentation, delayed uptake, or non-utilization of cataract surgery or related services. Results: Twenty-six studies published from 1991 to 2024 were included.

papers.title: Thermal analysis of ternary hybrid nanofluids for advanced cooling of AI chips and data centers using dual numerical techniques
papers.abstract: The problem of controlling the massive heat produced by high-performance AI processors has become more difficult due to the quick development of artificial intelligence (AI) and the exponential expansion of data centers. In addition to reducing processing efficiency, excessive heat endangers system dependability and energy sustainability. To mitigate this challenge, the present study investigates the application of ternary hybrid nanofluids (Tri-HNF: Al₂O₃–CuO–GNP/EG) as advanced coolants, comparing their performance with binary hybrid nanofluids (Di-HNF: Al₂O₃–CuO/EG) and mono nanofluids (NF: Al₂O₃/EG) in enhancing thermal regulation over a flat surface. The Collocation Chebyshev Method (CCM) and the Galerkin-weighted residual Method (GWRM), two separate numerical techniques included in Mathematica 11.3, were used to convert the governing nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) to ordinary differential equations (ODEs) and solve them numerically. The excellent agreement between the two methods demonstrates the consistency and accuracy of the numerical schemes. The effects of magnetic field, viscosity, suction, radiation, and heat generating factors on the flow and temperature fields were revealed using parametric experiments. Findings show that the Tri-HNF exhibits superior thermal performance due to the synergistic effects of Al₂O₃ (enhanced stability), CuO (excellent thermal conductivity), and graphene nanoplatelets (GNP) (exceptional heat transport efficiency). Compared to Di-HNF and NF, the Tri-HNF achieves higher Nusselt numbers, improved heat dispersion, and lower thermal resistance. In summary, this work demonstrates that Tri-HNF provide an efficient and reliable solution for cooling AI chips, microelectronics, and data centers, offering a pathway toward sustainable and thermally stable next-generation computing systems.

papers.title: Bio-Briquettes Derived from Fibrous Agricultural and Softwood (FAS) Residues: A Review on Production Methods, Effects of Chemical Components, Utilization Potential, and Future Outlooks
papers.abstract: Fibrous Agricultural and Softwood (FAS) residues represent abundant lignocellulosic resources for bio-briquette production, yet their potential is strongly influenced by feedstock characteristics, chemical composition, processing conditions, and application requirements. A structured narrative review of 106 publications was conducted to synthesize these interrelationships and identify development prospects. FAS bio-briquette performance is governed by interactions between feedstock composition and processing conditions, with lignocellulosic fractions and ash-forming minerals determining the balance among mechanical integrity, energy performance, and combustion behavior. Various FAS residues, including rice husk and straw, corn cob, sugarcane bagasse, coconut and oil palm residues, cocoa pod shell, fruit and nut residues, pine residues, and softwoods have been investigated under diverse processing conditions. Reported properties varied widely with densities of 0.30–1.32 g/cm3, calorific values of 12.41–31.51 MJ/kg, moisture contents (MC) of 0.3–29.72%, ash contents of 0.1–59.2%, volatile matter (VM) of 0.9–90.7%, fixed carbon (FC) of 22.97–81.73%, compression strength of 0.004–21.75 MPa, ignition times of 10.25–106 s, burning rates of 0.119–5.85 g/s, and burning times of 23.88–84 min, while shatter resistance >99% and shatter indices 0.56–2.49%. Beyond domestic cooking and heating, FAS bio-briquettes show potential for coal co-firing, metallurgical reduction, and construction-material applications through ash utilization, although suitability depends on application-specific trade-offs. Future development should prioritize feedstock-specific optimization, scalable production, techno-economic and life-cycle assessment, and standardized quality and sustainability criteria for reliable commercialization.

papers.title: Effect of continuous high thermal processing on physico-chemical and nutritional alterations in cold-pressed and refined edible oils
papers.abstract: Background Continuous high thermal processing of edible oils induces significant physicochemical and nutritional alterations, influence their safety, stability, and consumer acceptability. Cold-pressed oils are generally perceived as nutritionally superior, but their oxidative stability under continuous heating remains less understand compared to the refined oils. Methods Twelve edible oils (7 cold-pressed and 5 refined oils) were collected and subjected to the continuous high thermal processing at 230 ± 5 °C for 0, 1, 2, and 4 h. Fatty acid composition, peroxide value, saponification value, free fatty acid percentage, acid value, iodine value, conjugated dienes, conjugated trienes, refractive index and colour were analysed. Results Among the oils available in the both cold-pressed and refined types, cold-pressed groundnut, sunflower, rice bran and palm oil retained more polyunsaturated fatty acids at 1 h, but showed greater losses after 4 h then their refined types. Soybean oil exhibited a sharp rise in trans fatty acids (0.76 to 5.88%), whereas, coconut oil remained lowest (0.38%) at 4 h. Peroxide value increased in refined sunflower oil (7.60 to 15.81 mEq O 2 /kg), but refined and cold-pressed rice bran oil declined to 0.01 mEq O 2 /kg in after 2 h. Free fatty acid and acid values decreased variably across oils. Iodine value reduction was highest in coconut oil and minimal in soybean oil (6.72%). Saponification peaked in coconut oil (321 ± 0.68 mg KOH/g) and lowest in cold-pressed sunflower oil (213 ± 0.83 mg KOH/g). Conjugated triene rose steadily but remained below diene, while progressive darkening (L* reduction) was observed in all oils. Heating for 1 to 2 h impacted the saturation of fatty acids, while 4 h can increase the risk of trans fatty acid and dienes/trienes formation. Conclusion Continuous high thermal processing compromises the nutritional and oxidative stability of edible oils. Coconut oil showed minimal alterations, while soybean oil and sesame oil were highly susceptible. These findings highlight the need for cautious thermal application in cooking practices to preserve oil quality.

These findings highlight the need for cautious thermal application in cooking practices to preserve oil quality.

papers.title: Modifying Airbus A220S Fuel Tank by Electrical Heating Unit for Use of Neat Biodiesel as Aviation Fuel Without Freezing Problem
papers.journal: Düzce Üniversitesi Bilim ve Teknoloji Dergisi
papers.abstract: In this study, an active thermal management system was developed to optimize the integration of Waste Cooking Oil (WCO) biodiesel into the Airbus A220 platform to reduce the carbon footprint in the aviation sector. Biodiesel’s Cold Filter Plugging Point (CFPP), which is disadvantageous compared to Jet A-1 and is set at -5 °C, poses a risk of fuel flow interruption during high-altitude operations (-56.5 °C outside air temperature). To counter such a probability, the 9.8 cubic meters (15,000 lb) fuel tank in the center of the aircraft was modeled in a 3D environment, consisting of a structure made of Aluminum 6061, along with copper heating elements spaced 90 mm vertically. The thermal performance of the developed system was evaluated using high-resolution 3D steady-state thermal analyses in ANSYS Mechanical. In the numerical analyses, a constant surface heat flux of 500 W/m² was applied in the regions where the heating cables are in contact with the tank surface. Under International Standard Atmosphere (ISA) conditions, the analysis results at the cruising altitude of 41,000 ft indicate that the system can safely sustain the fuel temperature above the critical CFPP of -5 °C. In addition, a worst-case scenario representing the possible failure of the heating system was defined to evaluate the operational limits of the fuel tank. Contour plots indicate that the fuel tank temperature is within safe operational limits. The study results show that active fuel tank heating systems enable WCO biodiesel to be used as a sustainable alternative fuel in modern regional jets.
papers.summary: In this study, an active thermal management system was developed to optimize the integration of Waste Cooking Oil (WCO) biodiesel into the Airbus A220 platform to reduce the carbon footprint in the aviation sector. The thermal performance of the developed system was evaluated using high-resolution 3D steady-state thermal analyses in ANSYS Mechanical. The study results show that active fuel tank heating systems enable WCO biodiesel to be used as a sustainable alternative fuel in modern regional jets.
